title: Retention and disk safety: the janitor, the disk budget, store caps, blob GC, quotas and the fill-past-cap test
description:
## Goal
Make "every growing store is capped" and "safe defaults" enforceable: one janitor for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint; a disk budget (amber at 80 %, `storage_full` at 95 %, reads and deletes always work); quotas that stop a looping agent; and a test that fills each store past its cap and shows it back under. This chain sets Slice 1's date (decision 41).

## Scope
- [ ] Janitor framework (`pf-janitor`): `JanitorJob` trait + registry, scheduler (hourly/daily jittered/weekly/monthly, one job at a time, ≤ 1,000 rows per transaction), reference-safety guard run inside the writer (never deletes anything a live or binned part references), `janitor_runs` rows in `/data/insights.db`, metrics, admin "run now".
- [ ] Main-DB jobs: events 30 d, build logs (last 20 builds per part, 30 d; clears `log_hash`), runtime errors 30 d (the 1,000-per-part trigger exists), audit yearly segments, idempotency 24 h, scratch expiry → bin (+ part epoch bump), bin purge at 30 d keeping the name as a tombstone.
- [ ] Data-snapshot retention (daily keep 7, hourly keep 48, on-demand not counted, keep the last one after 90 idle days until the part leaves the bin), scheduled-export rotation (keep `backup.export_keep`, never the only one), WAL checkpoint on both DBs + monthly `VACUUM` when free pages > 20 %.
- [ ] Blob GC: mark from every reference (version files and manifests, build files + br, build output and log, `build_deps.blob_hash`, drafts, data snapshots, assets, kept image tarballs, `shared_blobs`, `mirror_cache`, unexpired screenshots); sweep sets `unref_since`, deletes after a **7-day grace**; blobs written after the mark began are never swept. Shares the mark function with export.
- [ ] Disk budget: `[disk] budget_percent` (default 80 % of the volume, bounded); used = `/data` + runner images + BuildKit cache (0 until the runner exists); measured every 30 s plus counters on blob put/delete, never `du` on the hot path. States ok / warn ≥ 80 % / full ≥ 95 % of the budget. In `full` the writer refuses versions, assets, builds, deploys and `/_rt` writes with `storage_full` (507, exit 7); reads, deletes, grants and revocations continue. Replaces the blob store's own volume check so there is one rule.
- [ ] Store-cap registry `{name, size_fn, cap_bytes, retention}` rendered on Health (amber ≥ 80 %, red ≥ 100 %) with the budget row; safe-defaults registry `{name, config keys, unsafe_key}` (secure headers, rate limits, quotas, container template, nightly export, ingress TLS, log redaction, retention caps): turning one off without `[unsafe] <name> = "off"` fails `config check` (exit 2, naming the key); with it, a Health warning. Caps only within declared bounds.
- [ ] Quotas enforced in the writer, below the registry, on every surface: per space (default 2,000 parts, 20 GiB, 1,000 versions a day) and per agent connection (500 versions a day, 2 GiB introduced), NULL = default, unlimited only with `[unsafe] quotas = "off"`. `quota_exceeded {kind, limit, retry_after?}` (429, exit 6); one deduplicated Health entry per principal/kind/day; `pf_quota_hits_total`.
- [ ] Retention test: one fill-past-cap case per existing §5h store, plus a completeness check against the registry so a new growing store without a cap and a case fails.

## Plan refs
§5h Disk safety, §5d Maintenance and Quotas, §5c data snapshots, §3e the bin, §5e (`janitor_runs`, GC sources), §4b errors; definition of done item 6; decisions 33, 41, 48.

## Considerations
- Quotas key on the connection, not the token (tokens rotate hourly), and are checked inside the single writer (race-free). A rejection stores no idempotency row; `retry_after` only for the daily window.
- Binned parts count toward quotas until purged. Bin purge never touches blobs; GC does, after its grace (which covers have/need uploads, long builds and a running export).
- Later stores (Insights, traces, logs, backend rings, images, BuildKit cache) register their own jobs and retention rows when they land.
- `build_deps` rows (round 3) cascade with their build, and their `blob_hash` is a GC reference.
- Per-connection quotas against a real agent token are proven again by the security suite in the Shipping bead.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/{janitor_e2e.rs::full_cycle_on_fixture, jobs_main_db.rs, jobs_snapshots.rs, jobs_exports.rs, blob_gc.rs, retention_table.rs::fill_past_cap::<store>}`; `crates/partifactory/tests/storage_full.rs`; `tests/e2e/disk_full.spec.ts` on a small loopback volume; quota loop test.
- Logs asserted: `event="janitor.job" store=<s> action=<a> items=<n> freed_bytes=<b> outcome="ok|error"`, `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"`, `event="op.done" op="part_create" outcome="storage_full"`, `outcome="quota_exceeded"`. Metrics `pf_disk_budget_bytes`, `pf_disk_used_bytes`, `pf_disk_budget_state`, `pf_quota_hits_total`.

## Verification gate
1. Binary from `main` in the e2e harness: each existing store filled past its cap comes back under after a janitor cycle (`janitor_runs`, Health rows); at 95 % of a loopback volume's budget `part_create` gets 507 while a delete, a read and the wrapper work, and Health shows red; a 10k-create loop stops at `quota_exceeded`.
2. CI green on `main` with the tests above (nextest job) and `disk_full.spec.ts` (e2e job).
3. Logs checked: `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"` and `event="janitor.job"` lines asserted.
4. The full e2e suite, every earlier gate included, still passes.
5. Close with SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts and the Health screenshot; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded via `br gate report`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each job frees the expected items on a fixture; a blob referenced only by a binned part survives; `janitor_runs` and /metrics show the bytes freed
- [ ] A test job registered through the trait runs on schedule and writes a `janitor_runs` row and metrics.
- [ ] The guard keeps a candidate referenced only by a binned part.
- [ ] A panicking/failing job records `error` and the scheduler continues.
- [ ] `/data/insights.db` is created on first start with the schema; `janitor_runs` rows land there; `partifactory.db` has no `janitor_runs` table (schema test).
- [ ] On a fixture each job frees exactly the expected rows; a 31-day-old event is pruned, a 29-day one kept.
- [ ] Only the newest 20 builds' logs per part remain referenced.
- [ ] Purged part names stay reserved (tombstone); undelete at 29 d ok, 31 d fails.
- [ ] Each job writes `janitor_runs`.
- [ ] A daily part keeps exactly 7 scheduled snapshots; hourly keeps 48; on-demand ones aren't counted.
- [ ] After 90 days idle exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin.
- [ ] A fresh install's nightly export dir holds exactly 7 files.
- [ ] Checkpoint and VACUUM run, VACUUM only above 20 % free pages; `janitor_runs` rows with `checkpoint`/`vacuum`.
- [ ] At 95 % of the budget a create returns `storage_full` while a delete and a read succeed; a store at 80 % of its cap shows amber on Health; switching rate limits off without the explicit key fails `config check`
- [ ] At 95 % a create returns `storage_full` while a delete and a read succeed.
- [ ] Warn state at 80 % appears on Health.
- [ ] Every write class listed is refused in `full`; every allowed class succeeds.
- [ ] A store at 80 % of its cap shows amber on Health.
- [ ] Switching rate limits off without the explicit key fails `config check`; with it, Health shows a warning.
- [ ] Caps outside bounds are rejected by `config check`.
- [ ] Every §5h row whose store exists has a passing fill-past-cap case; adding a growing store without a cap and a case fails the test
- [ ] An unreferenced blob is deleted after the grace period; a blob referenced by any version is never collected
- [ ] A loop of 10k creates stops at the quota with `quota_exceeded` and one Health-page entry
- [ ] A scratch part past `expires_in` moves to the bin and its caps die (part epoch bumped).
- [ ] A blob written after the GC mark phase began is never swept in that run; a re-referenced `unref_since` blob is cleared.
- [ ] `build_deps` rows are deleted with their build (cascade), and a blob referenced only by `build_deps.blob_hash` is never collected.
- [ ] Quotas apply identically on MCP, HTTP and the CLI (enforced below the registry), keyed on the agent connection, not the token; NULL means the default and unlimited needs `[unsafe] quotas = "off"`; a quota rejection stores no idempotency row.
- [ ] Every existing store appears on Health with size against cap, next to the disk budget row; no `[unsafe]` key is set in the default config.
- [ ] GATE: on the binary from `main` in the e2e harness, the fill-past-cap run fills each existing store past its cap on the running server and shows it back under after a janitor cycle (`janitor_runs` rows and Health store rows).
- [ ] GATE: on a loopback volume at 95 % of the budget, `part_create` gets 507 `storage_full`, a delete and a read succeed, the wrapper still opens a part, Health shows the red budget row; a 10k-create loop stops at `quota_exceeded`.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `crates/pf-janitor/tests/*`, `crates/partifactory/tests/storage_full.rs` (nextest job) and `tests/e2e/disk_full.spec.ts` (e2e job).
- [ ] GATE: the e2e run asserts `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"` and `event="janitor.job"` lines.
- [ ] GATE: the full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: closed with commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command excerpts and the Health screenshot path; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded with `br gate report`.

title: P2b Invites: native invites and local passkey accounts, then the Authentik provisioner
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Let the admin invite people who aren't users yet. First the vendor-free default: partifactory's own invite links that create local passkey accounts, so a deployment with plain OIDC (or no IdP) can invite anyone. Then the Authentik provisioner for the example deployment, starting with a permission gate against the real IdP that decides how much of it ships.

## Scope
- [ ] Invite tokens at `parts.<domain>/i/<id>`: kinds `single`, `multi` ("up to N people"), `email`, `recovery`; counted uses, status `sent -> opened -> enrolled | expired | revoked`, 7-day default expiry, one-click revoke, a cap on outstanding invites, enrolment rate-limited per invite and per IP.
- [ ] Local passkey accounts (`webauthn-rs`, discoverable credentials, conditional UI): "What should we call you?" -> Create passkey -> land on the part with the invite's grants applied. Passkey-only; no password path exists.
- [ ] Recovery: "Send a new passkey link" on an existing person (single-use, bound to the account, revokes the old passkeys). Linking a local account to an IdP identity (sign in with OIDC once while signed in locally).
- [ ] Local `pf-*` groups ("Make a group for this"), the invite UI in the share sheet and Admin -> Invites, `part_link_for {action: "invite"}` returning `#share=invite`.
- [ ] Cleanup lists: invitees who never enrolled, people inactive for 180 days, one-click remove with a 10 s undo.
- [ ] The device approval page offers to register a passkey for next time once local accounts exist.
- [ ] Authentik provisioner gate (`partifactory provision --gate`): try each forbidden operation and expect 403, record `[idp.provisioner] tier = A | B | C` in site config.
- [ ] Authentik invites: `/i/<id>` -> the `partifactory-invite` flow (invitation -> one field -> passkey enrolment -> user write into a holding group -> login); grants and `pf-*` memberships applied by API after enrolment; the IdP invitation deleted at the Nth enrolment.
- [ ] Authentik extras per tier: add by email (the IdP sends the mail), IdP recovery links, IdP-side `pf-*` groups; tier B/C paths hand the change to `provision`.

## Plan refs
§3a Invitations, the admin section (provisioner least privilege), UX click budgets; §4a.6 Invites; §5c provisioner gate; §5e `invites`, `invite_enrolments`, `passkeys`, `users`; §5f Invites + accounts row; §6 P2b; §6a P2b; §7 Identity and admin; decisions 23, 34.

## Considerations
- Inviting and creating groups are outward, admin-only actions with step-up; agents only hand over the `#share=invite` deep link (decision 34). No agent op creates an invite or group.
- Use counts live in partifactory for every kind (native invites have no IdP; Authentik invitations have no use count). Increment inside the single writer so concurrent enrolments on a multi-use link can't overshoot `max_uses`; the CHECK is a backstop.
- Multi-use links exist because single-use links pasted into family chats lose a race. Used or expired links show one plain page that doesn't reveal the part.
- `rp.id` is the apex, as for step-up. Local accounts count in `everyone-signed-in` and are what the IdP-less portability pass runs on.
- Recovery binds to the existing account and revokes the old passkeys in the same transaction, so no zombie account appears and a stolen device stops at once. IdP recovery keeps the same `sub`, so grants keyed on it survive.
- Removal is a revoke, not a delete (`users.status = 'removed'`, epoch bumps, agent connections revoked by the same cascade); undo re-grants from the audit rows.
- Authentik facts (checked 2026-10-23): invitations can't set groups, and have no use count. Unverified items (object-level permission names, `is_superuser` protection, blueprint-over-API, recovery-link permission) are gate items, not assumptions. Every runtime IdP write respects the recorded tier; the UI hides what the tier excludes. The `state` parameter binds the login to the invite; a mismatch or replay grants nothing.
- partifactory never sends email; "By email" shows only with a provisioner. Site config (the gate report, flow names) is private; the public repo ships the gate code and a report template.

## Order inside the phase
Native invites and local accounts -> cleanup lists; then the Authentik provisioner gate -> Authentik invites -> Authentik extras. Needs the Authentik adapter and `provision` from the rest of P1.

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the e2e harness with no provisioner: the admin mints an invite from the share sheet (Chromium, virtual authenticator), a new person on webkit-mobile creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out on the next request. With the Authentik provisioner on staging: an invited email enrols and an IdP removal locks them out within a minute.
- CI green on `main` with the invite e2e specs in the harness job and the portability lane (IdP-less pass).
- Logs checked: `event="invite.enrolled"` and `event="epoch.bump"` lines asserted by the e2e run; the gate report lists each forbidden operation and its status.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, the gate commands and output excerpts, engine and simulator runtime versions for the invite pass on `webkit-mobile` and in the iOS Simulator (the real-phone acceptance is the non-blocking human-checks bead's); `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Gate report in site config lists each forbidden operation and its observed HTTP status
- [ ] With no provisioner configured, an invitee creates a passkey (virtual authenticator) and lands on the part already granted; status moves sent->opened->enrolled; the N+1th use is refused; a recovery link keeps the same account and grants and revokes the old passkey
- [ ] Status transitions sent→opened→enrolled; N+1th use refused; expired and revoked links refused.
- [ ] Invitee creates a passkey with the virtual authenticator and lands on the part already granted; can sign in again later with the passkey alone.
- [ ] Recovery keeps the same user id and grants and revokes the old passkey (old passkey assertion fails).
- [ ] Linked account signs in via OIDC and keeps its parts and grants.
- [ ] Click budget: Share → "Invite someone" → Copy link (+ step-up).
- [ ] `part_link_for {action: "invite"}` returns the deep link; the link grants nothing (non-admin sees the sheet without the option).
- [ ] No agent op can create an invite or group on any surface.
- [ ] With the Authentik provisioner on, an invitee enrols with a virtual authenticator through the IdP and lands on the part already granted; the Authentik invitation is deleted at the Nth enrolment
- [ ] A recovery link keeps the same `sub` and grants; tier-B/C paths hand the change to `provision`, run by the admin, instead of calling the IdP
- [ ] Fixture users appear in the right list and removal revokes their grants with audit rows
- [ ] With no provisioner, the admin mints an invite link, a new person creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out at once; with the Authentik provisioner, an invited email enrols and removing them in the IdP locks them out within a minute
- [ ] Local accounts are passkey-only (no password path exists anywhere), and the IdP-less portability pass signs in with them.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `invite` in `part_link_for` in the same change that ships it, and the /skill.md regeneration test passes.
- [ ] The invitee flow (name, Create passkey, land on the part) also runs in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator where WebKit allows a software authenticator, recorded as `verified` evidence; the real-phone invite acceptance is the human-checks bead's and never blocks.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build in the e2e harness with no provisioner: the admin mints an invite from the share sheet, a new person on webkit-mobile creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out on the next request; with the Authentik provisioner on staging, an IdP removal locks them out within a minute.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the invite e2e specs in the harness job and the IdP-less portability lane pass.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="invite.enrolled"` and `event="epoch.bump"` lines; the provisioner gate report is recorded.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command output, engine and simulator runtime versions) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

title: Builds: the build child, Slice 1 kinds, mirror-on-build, build_deps and the shared blob host
description: ## Goal Turn a committed source version into a build record and servable output, safely, for the four Slice 1 kinds (`html`, `markdown`, `text`, prebuilt `files`). Every kind is built, so `live` only ever moves through an `ok` build and a broken save never replaces a working page. Mirror-on-build makes Claude-written CDN `
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A build that panics, hangs or exceeds memory marks the build failed/timeout, the server keeps serving, and `live` is unchanged; `wait:true` returns within 2 s or `build.status=running`
- [ ] Panic, infinite loop, and 2 GiB allocation fixtures each yield `failed/builder_crashed`, `timeout`, `failed` respectively, within deadline + 100 ms.
- [ ] Pool size formula verified for 1, 2, 4, 16 cores.
- [ ] A killed worker is replaced; subsequent builds succeed.
- [ ] Commit v1, v2, v3 quickly with one worker busy: v2 ends `superseded`, v1 and v3 build.
- [ ] Same source rebuilt (e.g. restore of v1 as v4, identical manifest) reuses output with no child spawn.
- [ ] Boot recovery re-queues stale `running` rows.
- [ ] Failed build of v3 leaves live at v2; ok build of v2 arriving after v3 is live does not move live back.
- [ ] `after_check` version with failed gate stays off live; with renderer absent goes live with `check_skipped`.
- [ ] `wait` returns within 2 s / 15 s bounds (test clock).
- [ ] `part.live_changed` emitted exactly once per switch.
- [ ] Each failure reason produced by a dedicated fixture; private IP via DNS rebinding fixture (first lookup public, second private) still refused because connection uses the vetted IP.
- [ ] jsDelivr `/gh/...` refused; `/npm/...` allowed.
- [ ] Floating resolution re-uses cache within 24 h (test clock).
- [ ] Golden fixtures: cdnjs `<script>`, Google Fonts CSS with woff2, jsDelivr `+esm` module importing further modules, CSS `@import` chain, srcset — output references only `blobs-part` URLs.
- [ ] Source manifest unchanged byte-for-byte.
- [ ] SRI mismatch fixture fails with `integrity_mismatch`.
- [ ] Kind detection: `index.html` → html, `*.md` → markdown, `*.txt` → text; `files` is never detected; a `.txt` part's raw output equals its input bytes exactly, with stable `L1..Ln` anchors; the golden render corpus is byte-stable across runs and machines.
- [ ] The entry HTML is stored with only the sandbox rewrites applied (no prelude tag, import map or `pf-boot` at build time).
- [ ] Each build with mirrored libraries writes `build_deps` rows: cdnjs, jsDelivr `/npm/`, unpkg and esm.sh URLs map to npm `name@version`; an unparseable URL is stored with ecosystem `unknown` and the URL as written; deleting a build deletes its rows (decision 48, provisional).
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` (dev feature) running in the e2e harness with the fake CDN, `partifactory dev put` builds an html, a markdown, a text and a `files` part to `ok`; their output references only `blobs-part` URLs; `mirror_cache` and `build_deps` rows are present; private-address and off-allowlist fixtures end `mirror_failed` with `live` unchanged; a fault-injection panic ends `builder_crashed` while `/healthz` keeps answering.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the `pf-build` unit, golden and integration tests in the nextest job (`ci/test.sh`).
- [ ] GATE: The run's server JSONL shows `event="build.finished"` for each build and `event="egress.refused" reason="private_address"`, with no file content or query strings logged.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite and every earlier bead's gate tests still pass.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, the dev commands and a `builds`/`build_deps` excerpt) and `br gate report` passes for `ci_green` and `verified`.

title: Updates and advisories: OSV matching, the advisory surfaces, part_edit update, auto-update
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Parts are built once and left alone, so partifactory must notice when a library a part carries gets a known vulnerability, say so where people and agents already look, and make the fix one call or one tap, without ever changing a live part by itself. Slice 1 already records each build's library list (`build_deps`, decision 48); this epic adds the advisory data, matching, the surfaces and the update paths for frontends. Backend image SBOMs and base-image digest checks belong to P2a.

## Scope
- [ ] Advisories spike first: measure the OSV bulk dump sizes for the ecosystems in use, matching speed against 10k `build_deps` rows, and pick Syft or Trivy as the runner's pinned scanner image (for P2a); sets the advisory-DB cap. Go/no-go note in `docs/spikes/advisories.md`.
- [ ] `AdvisorySource` adapter, chosen by `[advisories] source`: `osv-bulk` (default: daily download of `https://storage.googleapis.com/osv-vulnerabilities/<ECOSYSTEM>/all.zip`, incremental from `modified_id.csv`, stored under `/data/advisories/`, matched locally), `osv-api` (`POST /v1/querybatch`, sends only package names and versions; the config comment says so), `none` (a warning on Health and in `doctor`). Attribution stored and shown per record (CC-BY 4.0, CC0, MIT, Apache, CC-BY-SA for Ubuntu).
- [ ] Nightly matching against `build_deps` (and, once P2a lands, stored SBOMs) writing `advisories` rows (`part_id, build_id, ecosystem, package, version, osv_id, severity, fixed_in, first_seen, state open|fixed|ignored, ignored_by, reason`); `unknown` deps listed as such; inline code reported as "inline code isn't checked".
- [ ] Severity in context: OSV severity plus context; frontend advisories shown, not alarmed, raised one level when the part has a Can-contribute link or a backend; never a bare CVSS number.
- [ ] Surfaces: chrome badge for owner and editors (with Update libraries and Ignore…), counts on Health and in Insights (Parts page, by layer and severity, time open), `advisories` in `part_get`, `dep_advisory` warning in `part_check` and `build.warnings`, a `part.advisory` event, the ops webhook only for a critical advisory on a backend or a contribute-link part.
- [ ] Fix paths: `part_edit {rebuild: true, update: "patch" | "minor" | "latest"}` re-resolves recorded libraries within the range and builds a new version under the part's `live` setting; the Update libraries button (2 interactions, undo is the normal restore); ignore with a reason by a person or an agent with `parts:write`, audited.
- [ ] Auto-update (decision 49, provisional): `[advisories] auto_update = "never" | "patch"`, per part override; frontends default `never`; backends `patch` only with `fixed_in`, through `after_check`, rolled back automatically on a failed check, recorded as `system`. That rollback is a backend rollback, so it is code only and best effort (decision 51): it never touches volumes or runs migrations.
- [ ] Storage and retention rows (§5h): advisory DB latest sync only under a cap; SBOMs kept with their build under a per-build cap; `advisories` rows deleted with their build; the janitor covers all three and the retention test gains the rows. `/data/advisories/` is never exported.
- [ ] Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `update` on `part_edit` and `advisories` on `part_get` (item shape `{ecosystem, package, version, osv_id, severity, context, fixed_in, state, attribution}`) in the same change that ships them.

## Plan refs
§3h Updates and advisories; §4 op table (`part_edit`, `part_get`), Events; §4a.6 Part view (Advisories), Admin Health; §4a.7 budgets; §4b warnings; §5e `build_deps`, `advisories`; §5f Advisory data row; §5g Parts page; §5h rows; §7 Updates and advisories; decisions 44-49.

## Considerations
- Immutability stays the rule: old builds keep their frozen import maps and image digests, so rollback stays exact. An update is always a new version.
- `osv-bulk` is the default because only public data comes in and nothing goes out about what the household runs. With `osv-api`, nothing but ecosystem, package and version may leave (canary test).
- It fails open: a DB more than 7 days stale turns Health amber; builds never block on it.
- No approval queues and no notifications for people: a finding is a record, not a queue.
- Dump sizes and matching speed are unmeasured; the spike sets the cap and decides whether matching needs an index beyond `build_deps_pkg`.

## Order inside the phase
The spike → OSV sync and matching with its surfaces → `update` and the Update libraries button → auto-update. Backend SBOMs and base-image checks join from P2a.

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the e2e harness: a part built against a library with a seeded OSV fixture advisory shows the badge, the Health count, `advisories` in `part_get` and `dep_advisory` in `part_check`; Update libraries makes a new version that goes live under `after_check`, and restore undoes it.
- Each child bead's own gate observed; CI green on `main` with the advisories suites; logs checked: `event="advisory.sync"`, `event="advisory.match"` and the `part.advisory` event.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, `communal_pixel_editor` included, passes.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run ids, the spike note, a screenshot of the badge; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The advisories spike note records the OSV dump sizes for the ecosystems in use, matching time against 10k `build_deps` rows, the advisory-DB cap, and the Syft-or-Trivy choice for the runner, with the versions it ran on.
- [ ] With the default `osv-bulk` source the advisory DB syncs daily into `/data/advisories/`, incrementally after the first download, and nothing about parts leaves the box.
- [ ] With `source = "osv-api"`, the outbound requests carry only ecosystem, package name and version, never part content, names, titles or URLs (canary test).
- [ ] With `source = "none"`, Health and `doctor` show a warning.
- [ ] An advisory DB more than 7 days stale turns Health amber, and a build with the DB stale or missing still succeeds (fail open).
- [ ] Matching a seeded OSV fixture against `build_deps` writes an `advisories` row per affected build; an `unknown` dependency is listed as unknown, and the part's list says inline code isn't checked.

title: The op registry and core ops: part_create, part_edit, part_get, the HTTPS API and the part CLI
description:
## Goal
Define every agent-facing op once, in Rust, and render it as the HTTPS JSON API (with a truthful OpenAPI 3.1 document) and the `part` CLI, with one error catalogue written so an LLM can self-correct. Deliver the core ops behind them: `part_create`, the `part_edit` engine (ordered anchor edits, per-file compare-and-set, auto-rebase, idempotent replay, mode fields) and the `part_get` read path. MCP and discovery are later generated from the same registry, so nothing exists on one surface only.

## Scope
- [ ] Registry crate: `trait Op` (`NAME`, `SCOPE`, `HINTS`, `Output`, executable `examples()`, `run`), a registry macro, `Ctx` with the one `(person, connection, scopes, spaces)` principal, the Slice 1 op types exactly as in docs/agent-contract.md (`part_check`, `part_data`, `part_link_for` typed here, filled by their beads); `deny_unknown_fields` with "did you mean"; `request_id` format.
- [ ] One `OpError` catalogue with the §4b HTTP and CLI-exit maps; an op or error without description, hint and example fails the build; `insta` schema snapshots; non-object outputs wrapped for rmcp.
- [ ] HTTPS API on `:8080`: `POST /api/v1/{op}` (200 on success), GET aliases and `PUT …/files/{path}` with `If-Match` over the same handlers; pluggable bearer authenticator (dev token under the `dev` feature until agent connections land); 401 + `WWW-Authenticate`, 429 + `Retry-After`; JSON-RPC body gets the "MCP lives at /mcp" hint; bodies capped before auth (8 MiB request, 2 MiB source file, 25 MiB blob).
- [ ] Blob have/need (`POST /api/v1/blobs`, `POST /api/v1/blobs/missing`, `{path: {blob: sha256}}` in writes); `/openapi.json` via `aide` with a generated `Error.code` enum, an additive-only snapshot test and the GPT Actions lint.
- [ ] `part` CLI from the registry: `part <op> --json @file|-`, scalar flags, aliases `put` (file or dir), `get`, `edit --replace`, `check`, `help <op>`; one `request_id` per invocation reused on retry; token from env, keychain, then a mode-600 config file; §4b exit codes.
- [ ] `part_edit` engine: `replace`/`write`/`delete`/`rename` in order, all or none, byte-exact anchors occurring exactly once; §3d limits; anchor errors with `edit_index`, best-match context (Levenshtein ≥ 0.6, ±3 lines, ≤ 2 KiB), `lines`, `similarity`.
- [ ] Rebase inside the single writer (`base_unknown`, `invalid_against_base`, `if_match` against head, `rebased_from`), wrapped in the part service's idempotency layer: replay checked before anchors, a rejected write stores nothing.
- [ ] Mode fields, exactly one per call: `restore`, `delete` (`parts:delete`, epoch bump), `undelete`, `rebuild`, `meta` (no version; `shared_data_writers` audited, freeze hook); `wait` 2 s, or 15 s with `check`/`after_check`; `live` stored on the version; `check_skipped` while no renderer exists.
- [ ] `part_get`: version selection, `files`, `content` for parts ≤ 32 KiB, `file`/`range`, `history`, `diff`, `build: <id>` with its log, the latest 20 `runtime_errors`, `not_found` outside the connection's spaces.

## Plan refs
§3c; §3d Creation contract, Concurrency contract, Big files, `wait`; §4 op table, Slice 1 op fields, `part` CLI; §4b registry, Adapters, Errors; §5d body caps; docs/agent-contract.md "Calling ops", "The ops", "Errors", Rules 1-2; decision 11.

## Considerations
- `schemars` + `aide` (and rmcp's `schemars`) give one schema generator. `v1` is additive only: a breaking change is a new op name.
- An invisible part is `not_found`, never `forbidden`. A failed build is not an error (200, `build.status: "failed"`).
- One writer serialises commits, so versions are gap-free and rebase runs in the same critical section.
- CLI aliases are sugar and add no behaviour; the dev token works only on a `dev`-feature server.
- Round 3: `part_edit {update}` and `part_get` `advisories` come with the advisories work; the contract gains both then.
- MCP, `/skill.md` and four-driver conformance are the MCP, discovery and conformance bead.
- Blocked by the identity bead (the policy engine decides `not_found` and roles) and by the part host (`runtime_errors` rows come from its prelude, `delete` bumps its epochs). The wrapper bead runs in parallel; its chrome `summary` becomes a view over `part_get` once both have landed.
- `/api` registers its rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead); 429 + `Retry-After` come from it.

## Tests and logging
- Registry: `pf_ops::snapshots::schemas_match`, `catalogue::*` (+ a `trybuild` negative), `validate::unknown_field_suggests`, `examples::examples_roundtrip`.
- Engine: `pf_model::edit::tests` table, `prop::all_or_none`, golden best-match fixtures, `pf_model::rebase::tests`, `concurrent_editors.rs`, `part_edit_end_to_end.rs`.
- API/CLI: `openapi.rs`, `blobs.rs`, `errors.rs`, `gpt_actions_lint.rs`, `timeout_retry.rs`, `part_edit_wait.rs`, `runtime_errors_roundtrip.rs`; CLI `roundtrip.rs`, `exit_codes.rs`, `put_dir.rs`, `credentials.rs`, `request_id.rs`.
- Logs asserted: `event="http.request" route_class="api" op outcome` with `request_id`; `event="op" op="part_create" surface="cli"`; `event="part.edit" rebased_from`; no `event="blob.put"` on a second `put ./dist`; no content (canary).

## Verification gate
- On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness (dev token): `part put x.html --name packing` then `part get packing` returns the same bytes; a second `part put ./dist` uploads nothing; two disjoint edits from one base both commit; a retried timed-out edit returns `replayed: true`; `/openapi.json` validates as OAS 3.1.
- CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest job, the OpenAPI snapshot and the GPT Actions lint.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="http.request" route_class="api"` lines and zero `blob.put` on the second put.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts; `ci_green` and `verified` reported.

title: The rest of P1: edge, identity extras, workspace extras, Insights store, doctor, portability lane, bench
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Finish P1 "Edge + identity" beyond what Slice 1 shipped: adapters for the example deployment, the everyday workspace UI, the admin area, the Insights store with traces and logs, `doctor`, the portability lane that proves no vendor is required, and the honest performance comparison. P1 is done when the admin opens a part on a phone via SSO, the portability lane is green, a public link unfurls as a titled card from mobile data, the §7 checklist passes from outside, and the drill restores everything on a second host in under 15 minutes.

## Scope
- [ ] Titled public card: SVG template -> usvg/resvg -> 1200x630 PNG with bundled Plex fonts and rustybuzz wrapping, content-addressed `/og/<sha256>.png`; the root goes back to the content-free card when the last public link is revoked.
- [ ] Search: FTS5 over title, description, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 x recency; policy-filtered results.
- [ ] Workspace extras: versions rail (restore, compare, preview old), Bin view, search sheet, agent activity, Details sheet, install part as app, ⋯ extras (zip, Pin with a `pins` table), inward share rungs, Move to Family, Ask for access.
- [ ] `partifactory provision`: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, `manual` providers, ownership rules, dry-run, run log, `family` + `system` spaces.
- [ ] Cloudflare adapter (tunnel ingress + `tunnel` compose profile, DNS plugin, cache rules, one rate rule, fallback Worker, health probe) and the Authentik spike, then the Authentik adapter (60 s directory poll, cloned flows, invite flow, provisioner account).
- [ ] Optional ops-alert webhook, off by default, one signer shared with agent webhooks.
- [ ] Deliverable extras: nginx and Traefik configs, arm64, SBOM, cosign, example CI workflows.
- [ ] `partifactory doctor` with an exit-code table and hook slots (provisioner, runner firewall, advisories).
- [ ] Insights store (`insights.db`, its own writer, typed content-free events, salted viewer keys, rollups), request-id propagation + tail-sampled traces, the log pipeline (zstd segments, export/tail, push adapters), and the no-content-in-logs fuzz test.
- [ ] Admin area shell: tabs, step-up chip, Audit ledger, People/Groups/Agents, the `unsandboxed` toggle and list, owner change.
- [ ] Workspace PWA + the cross-page error-page e2e; visual regression suite; thumbnails endpoint and `views?` in `part_get`; the one-screen regrant UI.
- [ ] Portability lane: Dex pass, IdP-less pass, adapter-excluded build, vendor egress blocked, release tag gate.
- [ ] nginx + HAProxy comparison on the real content path (needs the regression bench, which the tsx and rest-of-P0 epic carries).

## Plan refs
§3 Topology and ingress; §3a identity, Ask for access, Admin; §3e Search; §4 ops alerts; §4a.6-§4a.7 screens and budgets; §4c Tier (a); §5a; §5b; §5c provision; §5d doctor; §5f portability lane; §5g Insights; §5h; §6 P1; §6a "The rest of P1"; §7; decisions 22-24, 32, 40, 42.

## Considerations
- Adapters never land before their generic default, and nothing outside an adapter may depend on its results. Authentik facts (checked 2026-10-23): invitations can't set groups and have no use count; conditional-UI passkeys need a WebAuthn validation stage on the identification stage (2025.12+). Spike results live in the private site repo; the public repo keeps a generic `docs/spikes/authentik.md`.
- Cloudflare: Free allows one rate-limit rule (IP only, 10 s), and it caches by file extension, so `blobs-part/b/*` and `parts/og/*` need "eligible for cache" rules. Part blobs are `private` and must never be HIT. Edge caching is never needed for correctness.
- Directory fail open: an unreachable IdP keeps last-known membership, marks it stale (`kv` `directory.stale_since`), never bumps an epoch, and alerts after 10 minutes (`idp_unreachable_10m`); a definite removal fails closed.
- Card inputs are fixed fields, never part content; separate private/public input types make the content-free guarantee a compile-time fact. The audience decides the card, never the User-Agent.
- Search indexes readable text, never code; notes and comments index through hooks the P2 work calls. No query text in logs.
- Insights never back-pressures serving: bounded channel, drop and count. No free-text fields, no raw IPs (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48, HMAC with a daily in-memory salt); `insights.db` already exists from Slice 1 (the janitor writes `janitor_runs` there), so adopt it, don't re-author the DDL. Request ids use one prefix, `r_`.
- Stdout always carries every log line; disk segments and push adapters can drop, stdout can't. OTLP logs use the `[otlp]` section (P4 adds traces and metrics to it).
- `/admin/*` answers non-admins with 403 (§7), never 404. The `/_pf/doctor` probe is byte-identical whether a part exists or not.
- The comparison runs off-hours on the deploy host; shared CI runners are too noisy to gate on. Results are tracked, not gated.
- Work that plugs in later without an edge: doctor's provisioner probe (P2b gate), runner-firewall check (P2a), advisory checks; the Insights store and log pipeline register janitor jobs and retention-test rows when they land.

search -> the workspace extras; `provision` -> the Cloudflare and Authentik adapters (Authentik spike first); `doctor` after the disk budget; the Insights store -> traces and the log pipeline -> the no-content fuzz test; the ops-alert webhook after Health and the disk budget; the deliverable extras -> the portability lane; the bench -> the nginx/HAProxy comparison; the titled card after the wrapper.

title: Spike: opaque-origin sandbox and wrapper flow on every browser engine (emulated and simulated)
description:
## Goal
Verify, in the first week and before the content listener starts, every browser behaviour the serving model rests on: each part document served with CSP `sandbox` (no `allow-same-origin`) runs in an opaque origin with no cookies, on its own host `<name>-part.<domain>`, framed by a trusted wrapper at the part host's root that gets its cap from a `#pf=` fragment, with admin step-up by WebAuthn with `rp.id` = the apex. Every engine is covered by emulation or simulation, so nothing here waits on a person or a phone: Playwright Chromium (desktop, and mobile emulation with the virtual authenticator), Playwright WebKit (desktop and a mobile profile), Playwright Firefox, and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator on the Mac. If WebKit or the simulator behaves differently, the part host, prelude and wrapper change now rather than after they're built. Items 10, 12 and 13 decide the wrapper flow.

## Scope
- [ ] A throwaway rig in `tests/sandbox-spike/` on a TLS test domain with an internal-CA wildcard cert: workspace host `parts.` setting a `__Host-` `SameSite=Lax` test cookie, part hosts `a-part.` and `b-part.`, a sibling `canary.` service that echoes received cookies and headers, and `blobs-part.`. Part responses carry the canonical CSP verbatim from §2 and answer `Origin: null` with `ACAO: null` + `Vary: Origin`, never `Allow-Credentials` or `CORP`. Every item is a self-reporting page that posts `{item, browser, ua, result, detail}` to a collector, so the same page runs under Playwright and under `simctl openurl`.
- [ ] Lanes: `run.sh` drives Playwright Chromium (`chromium-desktop`, `chromium-mobile` with a phone viewport, touch and the CDP virtual authenticator), WebKit (`webkit-desktop`, `webkit-mobile`) and Firefox (`firefox-desktop`), all in CI. `ios-sim.sh` drives Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`xcrun simctl boot`, `simctl keychain add-root-cert` for the rig CA, `simctl openurl` per item page, `simctl io screenshot` after each) locally on the Mac, or on a macOS runner if one exists; its `results.jsonl` and screenshots are attached as evidence.
- [ ] Items 1-9 (opaque-origin semantics), one page each: `'self'` matching; `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-*` values; fetch, module scripts and `import()` with `ACAO: null`; the `localStorage` redefinition visible to later scripts; blob workers and the relative-URL wrapper; popups escaping the sandbox, clipboard, `navigator.share`, fullscreen; `cookieStore.set` and `document.cookie` failing; no Lax cookies on fetch/POST to a sibling service or the workspace; `sandbox` honoured from the header but not from `Report-Only` or `<meta>`.
- [ ] Item 10, the wrapper flow (seven checks): no-cap `location.replace` to a stub `/grant`; the `#pf=` fragment surviving the 302; `history.replaceState` clearing it before any other script, never in `Referer` or logs; explicit part-host `frame-ancestors` admitting the same-host wrapper; a credentialed same-site `fetch` to the workspace carrying the Lax cookie, with WebKit's tracking prevention on (desktop WebKit, `webkit-mobile` and the iOS Simulator); the framed part failing to read `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage`; a `#share=public` fragment surviving the hop.
- [ ] Item 11 (Cloudflare adapter only): a wildcard CNAME to `<tunnel>.cfargotunnel.com` serves a new `*-part` name. Recorded as "not run: no test zone" and handed to the Cloudflare adapter work.
- [ ] Item 12: WebSocket (`Origin: null` handshake) and SSE under `/c/<cap>/api/` and `/_rt/events`, held 60 s with a 25 s heartbeat, through Caddy and draft nginx and Traefik configs; the proxy settings needed are recorded.
- [ ] Item 13: a passkey registered on `parts.` with `rp.id` = the apex, asserted from the wrapper origin: with the virtual authenticator on Chromium (desktop and mobile emulation), and in the iOS Simulator where WebKit allows a software authenticator (otherwise record what the simulator shows, and that the real-device confirmation sits in the human-checks bead). The Telegram in-app webview is approximated by the WebKit lanes and a WKWebView-shaped simulator page; the real Telegram result belongs to the human-checks bead and never blocks this one.
- [ ] `docs/spikes/sandbox.md`: the results table (one row per item per lane), each fail with its consequence and fallback, a go/no-go per design choice, and a short "needs real-device confirmation" list that the human-checks bead picks up.

## Plan refs
§5 Maturity check (spike items 1-13), §2 Serving a part (canonical CSP, `Origin: null`, framed expiry, known losses), §2 The link to post (first-open flow, chrome actions, CORS), §3 Isolation of agent-written JS, §3a Admin (rp.id = apex), §6a Spikes, decisions 10, 25, 36.

## Considerations
- Known risk areas: WebKit blob workers, WebKit tracking prevention on credentialed same-site fetches, WebAuthn in webviews. Fallbacks the plan already names: list the part host explicitly instead of `'self'` (item 1); a wrapper-flow failure reopens the hand-off design; a WebAuthn fail in a webview feeds decision 36 (set Telegram to open links in the normal browser; Hermes hints "open in browser"; the person-bound-link fallback stays rejected).
- Real phones never block anything (the admin's rule): the iOS Simulator and Playwright's mobile profiles are the gate; the real iPhone, Android and Telegram checks live in the non-blocking human-checks bead, which files any failure as a `bug` bead for the swarm.
- The simulator shares the Mac's network: resolve the rig hosts through `/etc/hosts` on the Mac and trust the rig CA in the simulator keychain, never with certificate-error flags. `simctl openurl` opens Safari; `simctl io <device> screenshot` records the page. Boot one device per iOS runtime that matters (the installed iOS 27 runtime first).
- `/_rt` deliberately has no `Sec-Fetch-Site` check: opaque-origin requests are `cross-site` even to their own host. Item 2 confirms the exact values the part host must accept.
- Confirm the known losses (service workers, remembered permissions, persistent IndexedDB, own-host `<a download>` names; `?dl=1` instead).
- The no-cap hop must be client-side: the server never sees the fragment.

## Tests and logging
- `tests/sandbox-spike/run.sh` / `run.ts` drives items on the five Playwright projects; `wrapper_flow.ts` (virtual authenticator for item 13 on Chromium); `longlived.ts` (WS + SSE for 60 s, logs disconnect reasons); `tests/sandbox-spike/ios-sim.sh` drives the simulator lane and collects its posts and screenshots under `target/sandbox-spike/ios-sim/`.
- Each item page posts `{item, browser, ua, result, detail}` to the collector, which appends `target/sandbox-spike/results.jsonl` (an `event="spike.result" item=<n> lane=<l> outcome=<pass|fail>` line each); a script renders the markdown table from it and fails if any lane × item is missing.

## Verification gate
- `docs/spikes/sandbox.md` merged with a go/no-go for the serving model and the wrapper flow, the results table, the "needs real-device confirmation" list, and a runnable rig (`tests/sandbox-spike/run.sh`, `ios-sim.sh`).
- Observed on every lane: the five Playwright projects (Chromium desktop and mobile emulation, WebKit desktop and mobile, Firefox) and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator each have a result for every item, with engine, OS and runtime versions and screenshots; item 13 has a virtual-authenticator result on Chromium and a recorded simulator result.
- The Playwright part of the rig runs green in CI (a `spike` job), with `results.jsonl` kept as an artifact; the simulator lane's `results.jsonl` and screenshots are attached to the `verified` gate report.
- Logs checked: `results.jsonl` holds an `event="spike.result"` line per item per lane, none `fail` without a consequence row in the note.
- No regressions: every CI job that exists still passes with the `spike` job added.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, the simulator lane output, screenshot paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.

- [ ] Items 1-9 have a result row per browser with version.
- [ ] Rig runs with `tests/sandbox-spike/run.sh` (Playwright Chromium with desktop and mobile-emulation projects, WebKit desktop and mobile, Firefox) and `tests/sandbox-spike/ios-sim.sh` (Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator via `xcrun simctl`); every item page is self-reporting, so both lanes post to the same collector.

title: P5 Later, only if needed: WASM backends, S3 export upload, semantic search, built-in ACME
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Four independent additions, each built only if it turns out to be needed: WASM component backends as an alternative to containers, an optional S3-compatible upload of scheduled exports, semantic search alongside FTS5, and built-in ACME DNS-01 for hosts with no proxy. Each has its own "done when" and none blocks another.

## Scope
- [ ] WASM component backends: only with an ADR naming a part that containers serve badly; same grant model and routing under `/c/<cap>/api/*`; every §7 Backends line green for the WASM kind.
- [ ] S3-compatible upload of the scheduled export (R2 is one example), behind config, plus `import --from s3://...`, exercised in the drill.
- [ ] Semantic search: embeddings beside FTS5 with hybrid ranking, off by default; FTS5-only behaviour unchanged when disabled.
- [ ] Built-in ACME DNS-01: a wildcard cert via a DNS provider plugin, for hosts with no reverse proxy; renewal before expiry.

## Plan refs
§3e Search ("Later, additive"); §3f (WASM as a later alternative); §5c Layer 3 optional upload; §5f Ingress + TLS and Backups rows; §6 P5; §6a P5; §9 Non-goals (WASM backends in v1).

## Considerations
- WASM backends are a v1 non-goal; the ADR rule stops speculative work. Escape attempts, LAN reachability, identity-header forgery and write-only secrets must all hold for the WASM kind.
- S3 stays an upload of a finished export file: a sink outbox on the save path, Litestream (v0.5 has no age encryption) and R2 as a built-in were rejected (`docs/plan-history.md`). Encrypt with age off-site; recommended default: refuse to upload an unencrypted full export unless an `[unsafe]` key allows it. No save ever waits on the bucket.
- Semantic search: `part_find` over 10k parts is under 5 ms p99 with FTS5; measure and record what hybrid costs, keep the FTS-only path as fast. The embedding index is a new growing store: it needs a cap and a retention-test row, or `doctor` fails.
- ACME is an adapter, never required; the default stays a reverse proxy. A failed renewal must never take the site down while the old cert is valid; alert at 14 days left.

## Order inside the phase
Each item on its own, after what it extends: WASM after P2a backends, S3 upload after export and the drill, semantic search after FTS5 search and agent notes, ACME after `provision` and the portability lane (§6a).

Per item, before closing it:

title: MCP, discovery, /skill.md and cross-surface conformance
description:
## Goal
An agent told only `https://parts.<domain>` finds and uses everything, on any surface. MCP is one of four front ends, all generated from the one registry, and `docs/agent-contract.md` is the single guide: the MCP `instructions`, the body of `/skill.md`, the top of `/llms-full.txt` and the OpenAPI `info.description`. One conformance scenario then proves MCP, HTTP, the CLI and the skill file behave identically with device-code and personal tokens (definition of done items 3 and 7).

## Scope
- [ ] MCP at `POST /mcp` on the workspace listener: `rmcp` (version pinned exactly from the rmcp spike), Streamable HTTP, stateless (spec 2026-07-28, compatible with 2025-11-25: `server/discover`, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`); `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/*`.
- [ ] Tools generated from the registry: name, description, `inputSchema`, object-rooted `outputSchema` (non-objects wrapped), annotations from hints; `structuredContent` + a one-line text rendering; errors as `isError: true` with the catalogue JSON; `unknown_field` with "did you mean".
- [ ] `ImageOutput` fields render as an image content block (PNG <= 1 MB, downscaled): `part_check`'s screenshot, asserted against the real renderer.
- [ ] Auth: the bearer middleware from agent connections; failures are HTTP 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` + a JSON body naming the ways to get a token (device code, personal token), never a tool result; scope errors are `forbidden {scope_needed}` results. PATs and device-code access tokens both work.
- [ ] `instructions` = the contract embedded at build time; `part://<name>` resources as projections of `part_get` (`part://recent` waits for `part_find`); `<untrusted_content>` wrapping when `contains_untrusted: true`.
- [ ] Discovery: Markdown `GET /` (`Vary: Accept`), `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` (served, not published), `/agents.md`, `/skill.md` (frontmatter `name: partifactory`, body = the contract), `part skill install`. No spaces, parts or people in any of them; no A2A card.
- [ ] The op-section regeneration test (generator owns each section's field table and `Errors:` line; examples parsed against the schema) and the GPT Actions lint.
- [ ] Conformance: `tests/agent_surfaces/scenario.yaml` over the Slice 1 ops, inputs taken from the contract's examples, run by four drivers (rmcp client, a client generated from `/openapi.json`, the CLI with `--json`, commands extracted from `/skill.md`) x device code and PAT; normalised results, errors and audit rows identical.

## Plan refs
§4b One operation registry, Adapters, the shared guide, Discovery, Auth for each kind of client, Errors, Conformance; §3b auth failures are 401; §3c resources, prompt-injection hygiene; §4c `part_check` image block; §5 rmcp; decisions 11, 38; Slice 1 definition of done 3, 4, 7; agent contract Discovery, Connecting, MCP.

## Considerations
- No operation depends on an MCP-only feature (no sampling, elicitation or notifications); instructions and resources add nothing the registry lacks. Every adapter iterates the registry, so a divergence is an adapter bug the suite must catch.
- The HTTP 401 is load-bearing: it is what triggers a client's OAuth flow once authorization code lands after Slice 1. Until then Claude Code and other MCP clients use a personal token as a static header (`claude mcp add --transport http partifactory https://parts.<domain>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN"`).
- `server.json` is served, not published: the public MCP registry doesn't support private servers.
- `/mcp` registers its row in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead), keyed on the principal; the rmcp version is pinned exactly from the rmcp spike note.
- Lines moved here because they need real connections: the screenshot URL is per connection, and no agent token can make a public link on any surface.
- `update` on `part_edit` and `advisories` on `part_get` are not in Slice 1; the contract gains both in the change that ships them.

## Tests and logging
- MCP: `tools_list_snapshot.rs`, `error_mapping.rs`, `stateless.rs`, `part_check_image_block_real.rs`, `auth_http_401.rs`, `instructions_equal_skill.rs`, `resources_projection.rs`, `untrusted_wrapper.rs`, `mcp_pixel_smoke.rs`.
- Discovery: `contract_sections.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `tests/agent_surfaces/blind_agent.rs`; CI job `gpt-actions-lint`; an optional non-gating nightly small-model run.
- Conformance: `tests/agent_surfaces/run.rs` (four drivers), `normalise.rs`; per run `target/e2e-logs/conformance/<driver>-<auth>.jsonl`, diff printed on failure.
- Logs asserted: `surface="mcp" op=... outcome=...` with `request_id`, `event="auth.reject" surface="mcp"`, no content or token canaries.

## Verification gate
- In the e2e harness against the binary from `main`, a real MCP client (`claude mcp add` with a personal token, or the rmcp test client) connects to `https://parts.pf.test/mcp` and runs create -> `part_check` (image block returned) -> edit -> `part_data list`; a missing token gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`.

- The conformance suite passes with 4 drivers x device code and PAT; a deliberate divergence fails with a readable diff.
- CI green on `main` with the MCP, discovery and conformance tests in the nextest and e2e harness jobs, plus `gpt-actions-lint`.
- Logs: the run asserts `surface="mcp"` op lines and `event="auth.reject"`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.

Closing it meets P0's "Done when".

## Scope
- [ ] `tsx` kind: `App.tsx`/`.jsx` default export, oxc (umbrella crate, `transformer` feature) + rolldown with in-memory inputs inside the build child, generated `#root` shell with the prelude inserted at serve time, errors as `{file, line, col, message}`, compile perf logging. esbuild-as-subprocess fallback behind the same child protocol.
- [ ] Library set `libset.toml` (`library_set_version` in the build cache key): react and react-dom 18.3, lucide-react, recharts, d3, lodash, papaparse, mathjs, three, chart.js, tone, plotly.js, xlsx (shartifacts' compatibility matrix, credited in `NOTICE`), seeded as shared blobs (`source = 'seed'`); CDN-URL aliasing to the set for the same major; `duplicate_library` warning otherwise.
- [ ] Frozen `import_map` in the build manifest, merged with the cap-prefix entries at serve time (author entries win except `/` and `/c/`); `part_edit {rebuild: true}` opts a part into the current set.
- [ ] Golden compile corpus `tests/golden/tsx/` (compat matrix + Claude samples) with a runner, and `tests/e2e/tsx_corpus.spec.ts` on Chromium and WebKit.
- [ ] `svg` kind (served as a sandboxed document with the canonical CSP; build work none beyond brotli) and `code` kind (syntect highlight into a read-only viewer shell with `#L<n>` anchors); bin codes `SVG`, `CODE`; golden `tests/golden/render/{svg,code}/`.
- [ ] Toolchain upgrade: on a new `toolchain_version` rebuild every live part in the background at low priority (a `library_set_version` bump only parts whose frozen map would change), never switch `live`; `partifactory toolchain report --json`, `pf_toolchain_rebuild_total{outcome}`, a `kv` summary Health reads.
- [ ] Sandbox compat corpus `tests/golden/sandbox-corpus/`: 30 Claude-written artifacts + 10 Vite builds rendered under the sandbox on Chromium and WebKit, explicit per-sample expected-failure lists.
- [ ] Same-machine regression bench: `partifactory bench` (blob warm p99, 304, entry document, shared blob, cap verify, `/grant`, small `part_edit`), results JSON, `--compare` fails on > 10 % regression; feeds the nginx/HAProxy comparison in the rest of P1.
- [ ] Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `tsx`, `svg` and `code` (kind enum, kinds table rows, `duplicate_library` and `cdn_unpinned` warnings) and drops them from "After Slice 1", in the same change; the `/skill.md` regeneration test stays green.

## Plan refs
§2 Kinds, Mirror-on-build (One library set, Import maps), Part version (Why build records); §3d The build worker; §5 Stack (TSX/JSX, Tests row: sandbox compat corpus); §5a Performance; §6 P0; §6a Right after Slice 1; decisions 20, 39.

## Considerations
- Pin oxc and rolldown exactly and vendor them: oxc is 0.x with breaking releases, and rolldown's semver promise covers its JS API, not the Rust crate. Renovate never automerges them. The Slice 1 compiler spike note decides the details and the fallback.
- The `FROM scratch` image has no esbuild; the fallback is dev/CI only unless the release image deliberately ships it (say which).
- Frozen import maps are the reproducibility guarantee: a server upgrade must never change which React an old part loads. Toolchain rebuilds only create build records; a person or agent opts in with `rebuild: true`.
- An SVG can carry `<script>`; it is safe only under the canonical sandbox CSP. Part SVGs are part blobs, never in `shared_blobs`. The prelude is injected into HTML only, so don't expect `blocked_load` rows from an SVG. External SVG references are CSP-blocked, not mirrored.
- syntect runs server-side so the viewer needs no JS; its syntax set version is part of `toolchain_version`.
- Bench numbers are tracked, not gated, on shared CI runners; release gates compare against the previous release on the same machine. The blob scenario asserts zero DB queries (reuse the content hot path's query counter).
- Toolchain-upgrade results go to the CLI and metrics; Health reads the `kv` summary.

## Order inside the phase
tsx compiler in the child → library set and aliasing → frozen import maps + golden corpus + contract; svg/code and the compat corpus in parallel; the toolchain-upgrade rebuild after the corpus; the bench beside them. Tailwind and shadcn (P3) wait for `tsx`.

title: P3 Claude compatibility: claude.use, Tailwind and shadcn, viewer uploads, the agent inbox
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Make anything Claude writes run here unchanged: `claude.use("db" | "user" | "comments" | "artifact")` in the prelude (including pages that save themselves), Tailwind and shadcn for Claude-written parts, viewer uploads, and an agent inbox so a comment addressed to the agent reaches the right one. The spec is shartifacts' compatibility matrix (credited).

## Scope
- [ ] `claude.use("db")` and the `/_rt` `db.*` ops over `data_docs` (collection ≠ `__storage`), with per-document `rev` compare-and-set and data leases (`data_leases`), exactly like Claude's `db`.
- [ ] `claude.use("user")` (the viewer only; guests answered locally as "Guest 4f2a" with no network call) and `claude.use("comments")` for page code, with `provenance`.
- [ ] `claude.use("artifact").publish(...)`: self-publish with compare-and-set against the running version, which must be head and live; `via = self_publish`; idempotent by `request_id`.
- [ ] Tailwind + shadcn: a spike measures prebuilt utility CSS vs the mirrored Tailwind v4 browser build vs build-time class extraction on a corpus, writes `docs/decisions/tailwind.md`, then the chosen mechanism ships; shadcn joins `libset.toml`; `cdn.tailwindcss.com` script tags alias with a `cdn_aliased` warning; goldens and reference screenshots.
- [ ] Viewer uploads: `assets.put` over `/_rt` (25 MiB each, capped before auth, counted against the space quota), served at `/_a/<id>` behind the cap, listed and deletable by agents via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`, an `asset.added` event.
- [ ] Agent upload URLs: `part_create`/`part_edit {upload: [...]}` returns 10-minute URLs bound to the connection; `{path: {blob: sha256}}` wiring; the Slice 1 rejection of `upload` removed.
- [ ] Agent inbox and steward: `part_inbox` op, `to_agent` routing to the steward, states `open -> claimed -> answered -> resolved`, "stalled" after 15 minutes with no new version, runtime-error spikes as inbox items; the steward changeable in the share sheet.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` sections for every new op and field, in the same change.

## Plan refs
§1 (Claude-artifact compatibility), §2 Runtime calls `/_rt`, §3a role x runtime matrix and guests, §3c In place (persistent state, self-editing parts, assets, agent inbox), §3d Data CAS + leases, §4 ops (`part_data`, `part_inbox`), §4b shared guide, §5e `data_docs`, `data_leases`, `assets`, §6 P3, §6a P3.

## Considerations
- One storage model: a `claude.use("db")` document is the same `data_docs` row `part_data {collection, doc_id}` reads. No second store. `db.*` was settled here, not in Slice 1 (`window.storage` is the Slice 1 data API).
- Guests are web consumers only: a guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) gets 403. Don't invent a `partifactory.user()`.
- Self-publish is CAS, not rebase: a page publishing itself has no anchors, so a stale publish is refused and handed the newer version.
- Tailwind options fail differently: (a) prebuilt CSS is huge and can't do arbitrary values; (b) the browser JIT works with runtime class names but costs JS on phones; (c) build-time extraction is smallest but misses runtime classes and must fit the build child's 10 s budget with no network. A stated hybrid is fine. Any generator is pinned and vendored, like oxc and rolldown; Tailwind and shadcn (MIT) go in `NOTICE`.
- `storage_full` at 95 % of the disk budget refuses `/_rt` writes, never reads or deletes. Failures reject with `PfError` using catalogue codes.
- Asset names are untrusted (provenance-labelled); assets belong to the part's data, survive edits and are in exports. Assets are a new growing store: add it to the retention registry and the fill-past-cap test.
- The inbox is work addressed to an agent, never something waiting on a person (decision 34). A revoked steward connection falls back to "no steward", shown. Recommended spike threshold: a new error fingerprint seen 3 times in 10 minutes.

## Order inside the phase
`claude.use` after shared data, comments and `/grant`; Tailwind and shadcn after `tsx`; viewer uploads; the agent inbox after comments and the event log (§6a).

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the harness: a page copied from a claude.ai artifact (using `claude.use("db")`, state persistence and self-publish) runs unchanged on chromium-desktop and webkit-mobile; a viewer's photo upload reaches the agent's inbox and `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`.
- CI green on `main` with the P3 specs in the e2e job, the Tailwind corpus goldens, and the conformance scenario extended to the new ops on all four drivers.
- Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="rt" op="db.set"`, `event="asset.added"` and the self-publish `outcome` lines.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command output, screenshot paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

- [ ] Self-publish with a stale version is refused with the newer version; a poll part works for every viewer while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a `claude.use("db")` document is the same row `part_data` reads

title: communal_pixel_editor: the Slice 1 acceptance test, in CI on emulated and simulated devices
description:
## Goal
`communal_pixel_editor` is the Slice 1 acceptance test and this bead is the Slice 1 exit. The pixel board exercises every risky layer at once (sandbox, caps, builds, agents, guests, live shared data, data rollback), so it passing end to end in CI on every PR, with the guest also run in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator, proves the core before anything is built on top. The bead closes when the plan's definition of done holds for everything a machine can observe; the by-hand run on the example deployment and the Telegram passkey test are the non-blocking human-checks bead's, and nothing here waits on them.

## Scope
- [ ] Fixture `tests/e2e/fixtures/pixel.ts`: boots the e2e harness (Dex, Caddy, internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`, render sidecar on), seeds Dex users (the admin, one household user), resets `/data`, captures logs to `target/e2e-logs/communal_pixel_editor/`. The board HTML is a fixture copied verbatim from `docs/agent-contract.md`'s worked session (with the fixed `load()` call), so contract and test can't drift.
- [ ] Agent half (MCP via the rmcp client and HTTP, parametrised): device grant with `client_id=part-cli`, `agent_name="Pixel test agent"`; the admin's Chromium context taps Allow + virtual passkey; `part_create {name:"pixel", kind:"html", live:"after_check"}` in one call; `part_check` with click + `wait_ms` + `eval_return`; `part_data list prefix "px:"` stays empty (overlay discarded); post `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`.
- [ ] Admin half on `chromium-desktop` with a CDP virtual authenticator (`rp.id` = the apex), and again on `chromium-mobile` (phone viewport, bottom sheets): sign in, open the part host (address bar clean, no `#pf=`), Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy with in-sheet step-up; later Roll back data (newest snapshot preselected, the `reason: contribute` one) and Freeze; the shared budget helper `tests/e2e/lib/budget.ts` counts clicks, presses and WebAuthn ceremonies.
- [ ] Guest half on `webkit-mobile`, signed out: open `/l/<token>`, `POST /l/<token>/go` returns a guest cap, tap a cell, the admin tab repaints within 1 s; after Freeze the guest's next write rejects with a `PfError` and the cell reverts. The same guest half runs in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh pixel-guest`: `simctl openurl` the `/l/` link, the page self-reports the paint, the harness asserts the admin tab's repaint, screenshot after Freeze); its output is attached to `verified`.
- [ ] Required CI job on every PR (`ci/e2e.sh` runs the same steps locally), runnable from the published compose file with `_FILE` secrets.
- [ ] The definition-of-done roll-up: every Slice 1 bead closed with evidence, the conformance, security, retention and drill reports attached, and the human-checks bead's items listed as "pending the admin, non-blocking".

## Plan refs
"Slice 1: what ships first" (scope, decided for the slice, definition of done); §6 P2 Done when; §3a Can contribute links; §4a.7 click budgets; §4c `part_check`; `docs/agent-contract.md` worked session; decisions 31, 35-43.

## Considerations
- No browser OAuth flow anywhere: the agent connects by device code (decision 37); approval happens in the admin's Chromium context.
- Live-update latency is measured from the guest's `/_rt` write response to the admin tab's repaint (polling the cell's computed style), with timestamps in the logs. Contexts are coordinated by explicit test barriers, never sleeps; the simulator guest reports through the collector, and the barrier waits on that post.
- Rolling back to the `contribute` snapshot (taken when the link switched) makes the board end empty: a deterministic assertion.
- The `#share=contribute` deep link is an extra variant: tap the agent's link → confirm = 2 (+1 biometric).
- Real phones never block anything (the admin's rule): definition-of-done items 2 (the by-hand run on the example deployment, on the admin's phone and a signed-out phone on mobile data) and 8 (the Telegram passkey test) moved verbatim to the human-checks bead. A failure there is filed as a `bug` bead for the swarm; it never reopens this one.
- The portability-lane run of this test arrives with the portability lane after Slice 1; the two old lines that require it are verified in the rest-of-P1 epic. The backend variant is P2a.

## Tests and logging
- `tests/e2e/communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts` (projects `chromium-admin`, `chromium-mobile-admin`, `webkit-mobile-guest`) and `tests/e2e/agents/pixel_agent.rs`; `tests/device/ios-sim.sh pixel-guest`; traces, HAR and screenshots on failure.
- Asserted in order: `op=part_create outcome=ok`, `event=render.job purpose=gate outcome=ok`, `event=live.switch`, `event=audit action=link.mode`, `event=stepup outcome=ok`, `event=cap.mint subject_kind=link dw=true`, `event=rt.op principal=guest:* op=storage.set`, `event=data.changed`, `event=data.restore`, `event=epoch.bump key=minter:link:*`, `event=rt.op principal=guest:* outcome=stale_epoch|forbidden`.

## Verification gate
- Observed in CI on `main`: the whole flow on the harness, agent by device code, admin on Chromium (desktop and mobile emulation) with the virtual authenticator, guest on mobile WebKit, budgets exact.
- Observed on the Mac: the guest half in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator paints, the admin tab repaints within 1 s, and the post-Freeze write is refused; posts and screenshots attached to `verified`.

title: The part host: caps, the content listener, the prelude and /_rt
description:
## Goal
Serve every part sandboxed in an opaque origin with no cookies, on its own host `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, authorised by a host-bound capability in the path, with blob paths that never touch the database. Also serve the shared blob host and the prelude, partifactory's small runtime that makes Claude-written pages (`localStorage`, `fetch('/x.json')`, workers) run unchanged, plus `/_rt/v1`, its one server endpoint, and the `runtime_errors` loop that tells agents their page is broken. This is the security model and the hot path; the pixel test, retention and conformance all run through it.

## Scope
- [ ] Caps per §2 (`v1.<kid>.<payload>.<mac>`, ≤ 300 bytes, daily HKDF keys accepting `kid` and `kid − 1`, deterministic 12 h windows, 60 s for `render`), DB-free verify, `EpochStore` (part, minter, global, boot floor bumped on every start), and `partifactory dev cap <name>` (dev feature) for gates before `/grant` exists.
- [ ] Content listener `:8081`: only `-part` labels; `/c/<cap>/` content with the §2 navigation/subresource re-grant rule (302 or 401 `X-PF-Reauth`), 404 for bad caps, Origin rules; route slots for the wrapper and `/l/`.
- [ ] One header set: the canonical CSP on every part document (`unsandboxed` drops only `sandbox`), ACAO `null` for `Origin: null`, never ACAC/CORP/`Set-Cookie`, `?dl=1`.
- [ ] Serve-time entry: prelude tag first in `<head>`, cap-prefixed import map, `pf-boot` (≤ 256 KiB, empty for link/render/guest).
- [ ] Hot path: live and build-manifest caches invalidated from events, ETag/304, brotli, mmap LRU, a test query counter.
- [ ] Shared blob host `blobs-part`: only `shared_blobs` hashes, `public, immutable`, ACAO `*`; seeding for the prelude and `pf-shell.css`.
- [ ] Prelude (≤ 12 KiB brotli): synced `localStorage` shim with write-behind and `sendBeacon`, memory `sessionStorage`, inert cookie, no `indexedDB`/`caches`, URL prefixing, blob workers, `window.partifactory`, `pf:regrant`; schema in `crates/pf-prelude/PROTOCOL.md`.
- [ ] `/_rt/v1` (text/plain, no preflight): personal `storage.*`, `refresh`, `errors.report`, role checks from cap claims; `runtime_errors` by fingerprint, ≤ 10/min/part, 1,000 per part.

## Plan refs
§2 Serving a part (canonical CSP, capabilities, errors, framed expiry, runtime calls, entry templating, the prelude, known losses, unsandboxed, why one hostname per part); §2 The core idea (shared vs part blobs); §3 Topology; §3c errors close the loop; §5a lean hot path; §5e `epochs`, `shared_blobs`, `runtime_errors`, hot-path rules; §7 Part hosts, Caching and blobs; decision 10.

## Considerations
- Starts only after the sandbox spike's go/no-go: items 1 (`'self'` in a sandboxed document; hence `frame-ancestors` spells the host out), 4 (`defineProperty` on `localStorage` before page scripts), 5 (WebKit blob workers), 9 (CSP from the header) and 10/12 decide details.
- `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` are deliberate: CSP here is an egress policy; the opaque origin protects the viewer. Never add `allow-same-origin`.
- Bad MAC → 404 so caps are not an existence oracle. Verify checks `e ≥ max(epoch[part], epoch[global])`. Constant-time MAC compare. The cap string never reaches a log (redaction by route and pattern).
- The only DB read under `/c/` is the entry's `pf-boot` (cached per cap, invalidated on personal writes). The response never depends on the User-Agent.
- `refresh` for `user:` subjects re-checks access with fixture users until the policy engine lands in the identity bead, then calls its decision API.
- The wrapper side of `pf:regrant` (the framed-expiry flow) is verified in the wrapper bead.
- `pf-caps` (format, keys, `EpochStore`, mint and verify) is owned here, but the identity bead runs in parallel (§6a) and its `/grant` mints caps with it. Reserve `crates/pf-caps/` through Agent Mail before touching it; whichever bead gets there first lands the crate exactly per §2 and the other reuses it.
- `/_rt/v1` reads and writes register their rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead) instead of hand-rolling one; the guest and per-IP numbers come from the public-links bead.
- The sandbox and prelude specs also run in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`, a local lane whose posts and screenshots are attached to `verified`). Real phones never block anything.

## Tests and logging

- E2E (Chromium, WebKit, Gecko): `tests/e2e/{content_listener_sandbox,prelude_storage,prelude_network,runtime_errors,kinds_render,mirror_zero_third_party}.spec.ts`.
- Logs: `event="cap.verify" outcome=…`, `event="serve.entry"`, `event="blobhost.serve"`, `event="rt.call" op=… outcome=…`; no line contains a cap.

## Verification gate
