title: part_check: the render sidecar, actions and the after_check gate
description:
## Goal
Agents see and validate their own work before anyone opens it. `part_check` renders a version in a sandboxed headless browser exactly as a viewer would, optionally clicks and types through it, and returns a screenshot, a `blank` flag, uncaught errors, console lines and failed loads. The same check is the `live: "after_check"` gate, so a page that builds but throws never reaches people between an agent's create and its fix. The renderer is optional and never on the save path.

## Scope
- [ ] Sidecar `partifactory-render` as a `render` profile service (off unless `[render] enabled`), added to the e2e harness compose now and carried into `deploy/compose.yaml` by the Shipping bead: `chrome-headless-shell` pinned by digest + Noto fonts, non-root, read-only root, tmpfs `/tmp`, 768m / 256 pids / 1 CPU, `json-file` 10m x 3.
- [ ] Isolation: only a Docker `internal: true` network; `--host-resolver-rules` maps `*-part` and `blobs-part` to the gateway; partifactory serves the content handlers on an internal-only `:443` with a self-signed cert generated at start, SPKI-pinned; headers byte-identical to the public listener.
- [ ] Chrome over CDP (`chromiumoxide`): on demand, stop after 5 min idle, circuit breaker, `pf_render_up`.
- [ ] Renderer caps: subject `render`, 60 s, read-only, pinned `v`; `/_rt` reads real shared data only with `data:read`, personal storage empty, writes to a per-job overlay later reads see and that is dropped at job end; no `data.changed` from it; `errors.report` stored with `source: render`.
- [ ] Queue `render_jobs`: concurrency 1, coalesced per part (5 s debounce; requested check/gate jobs joined, not dropped), one retry, fresh context per job, hard 15 s.
- [ ] Driver: mobile 390x844@2x / desktop 1280x800; wait for `partifactory.ready()`, 500 ms idle or `wait_ms`; `actions` (<= 20, first failure stops); collect errors (`error`, `unhandledrejection`, `blocked_load`, `csp`), console, failed requests, height, timing, blank; URLs with the cap removed.
- [ ] Op `part_check` (`parts:read`, the contract's pixel example), `GET /api/v1/screenshots/<id>` (same connection, 10 min, `private, no-store`), 30 per hour per connection, `renderer_unavailable` (503, exit 7).
- [ ] The gate: `versions.live_gate`, `builds.gate_check`, a `gate` job after an `ok` build; live moves only on `passed`; renderer off -> `skipped` + `check_skipped`; `part_edit {check: true}` folds `check` in; a `part_check` on a gating version returns that same check.

## Plan refs
§4c Tier (b) and `part_check`; §3d `live`, the live switch and `wait`; §4 Slice 1 op fields; §5e `render_jobs`, `live_gate`, `gate_check`; §7 Render sidecar; decisions 16, 43; agent contract `part_check`, `part_edit`, Rule 3, the worked session.

## Considerations
- Production-identical URLs, CSP and secure context are the point: a check's result is what a viewer gets. Mirror-on-build means parts need nothing third-party, so the internal network suffices.
- Read-only real data + discarded overlay (decision 43): a painted pixel shows in the screenshot, and click + `eval_return` proves the write path without painting anyone's board. The overlay lives in the content listener, so the prelude has no special mode. It rides on the shared-data `/_rt` storage ops and `part_data`.
- A connection without `data:read` must not see shared data in a screenshot either.
- Concurrency 1 and 30/h keep RAM bounded on a household box and stop a looping agent; the 30-per-hour limit is a row in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead), keyed on the connection.
- Only the requesting connection may fetch a screenshot; that per-connection check and the MCP image content block are verified in the MCP, discovery and conformance bead, which has real connections.

## Tests and logging
- Unit: action limits, the 98 % blank rule, queue coalesce / retry / breaker.
- Integration: `crates/pf-render/tests/sidecar_isolation.rs` (egress and LAN canaries, header parity, idle shutdown), `rt_render_overlay.rs` + proptest `render_cap_never_writes`, `driver.rs` over `tests/golden/render/`, `part_check_e2e.rs`, `part_check_op.rs`, `live_gate.rs`.
- Logs asserted: `event="render.job" purpose="check|gate" outcome`, `event="cap.mint" subject="render"`, `event="rt.op" principal="render" persisted=false`, `event="live.switch" gate="after_check" result="held|moved|skipped"`; never a cap. Artifacts under `target/e2e-logs/<test>/`.

## Verification gate
- Binary from `main`, sidecar up (`docker compose --profile render up`) in the harness: `part check` on a throwing page, a blank page and the pixel board returns the error, `blank: true` and a click + `eval_return` value, PNGs saved; `part_data list` is unchanged afterwards.
- An `after_check` version that throws stays off `live`; the fix goes live (worked session steps 3-5, against the running server). Profile off: 503 `renderer_unavailable`, `check_skipped`. Egress and LAN canaries from the sidecar fail.
- CI green on `main`: these tests in the nextest job, `part_check_e2e.rs` in the e2e harness job.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="render.job"` and `event="live.switch"` and finds no cap in the JSONL.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Close with evidence: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, screenshot paths.

- [ ] `docker compose --profile render up` starts the sidecar; `docker inspect` shows read-only root, non-root user, limits, internal network only, log limits.
- [ ] From inside the sidecar, `curl https://example.com` (egress canary) fails; a LAN canary fails.
- [ ] Chrome loads `https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<cap>/` via the internal listener with the canonical CSP header identical to the public listener's.
- [ ] Idle 5 min → Chrome process gone; next job restarts it.
- [ ] A render cap cannot persist any `/_rt` write (§7 Render sidecar line).
- [ ] Write then read in the same job returns the written value; after the job, `data_docs` unchanged and the overlay freed.

- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the nextest job and `crates/pf-render/tests/part_check_e2e.rs` in the e2e harness job.
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="render.job"` and `event="live.switch"` log lines and finds no cap in the captured JSONL.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, every earlier bead's gate tests included, still passes.

title: Identity: OIDC sign-in, the claims directory, the policy engine, /grant and admin step-up
description:
## Goal
People sign in with any OIDC provider, get the one cookie partifactory sets, and every request is decided by one provider-neutral policy engine. `/grant` turns "this signed-in person opens this part" into a cap for the part's host, and admin power comes only from a pinned subject plus a fresh native passkey assertion. This bridges the cookie world (the workspace) and the cookie-free part hosts, and underpins every sharing guarantee.

## Scope
- [ ] Generic OIDC client (`openidconnect`, discovery from `[idp] issuer`, confidential + PKCE S256, `state`/`nonce`); claim names from config; `/signin?return=<path>` (path-only), `/oidc/callback`, `POST /signout`, `POST /signout/everywhere`; users keyed by `(idp_issuer, idp_sub)`.
- [ ] Sessions: `__Host-pf_session` (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`), stored as sha256, 30 days sliding (12 h without a refresh token), refresh token encrypted with `PF_SESSION_KEY`; sign out everywhere bumps each `minter:sess:<id>` epoch; audited.
- [ ] Claims re-read directory: groups claim at login, refresh-token re-read every 15 min, `invalid_grant` ends the session, unreachable IdP keeps last-known membership (`directory.stale_since`, alert `idp_unreachable_10m` after 10 min, no epoch bump); membership diffs bump only affected `part:<id>` epochs; local `pf-*` groups.
- [ ] Policy engine (`pf-policy`): roles view < comment < edit < manage; effective = max(part, space grants), inherited live; agents = person's role ∩ scopes within consented spaces; `everyone-signed-in` = audience group + active local accounts; the role × runtime matrix incl. guests and `shared_data_writers`; grant API with one audit row per change, epoch bumps on revoke, expiry timer; denials logged as structured decisions.
- [ ] `/grant?part&path&mode=wrap|direct` (host derived from the name), sign-in page with the content-free card when signed out, `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` with no title, silent re-entry, and the regrant handler for `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant`.
- [ ] Admin pin (`[admin] subject`), `RequireAdmin`, `partifactory admin bootstrap`, `partifactory admin break-glass` (5 min, once).
- [ ] WebAuthn step-up (`webauthn-rs` 0.5, `rp.id` = apex): `stepup` passkeys, assertions from the workspace and every active sandboxed part-host origin, `sessions.stepup_at`, 10-minute `RequireStepUp` on the admin action list, `step_up_status` for the UI chip.

## Plan refs
§3a (layers, how people sign in, spaces, audience ladder, role × runtime, who may write shared data, admin), §2 Serving (hand-off, errors, framed expiry), §5e identity, access and `epochs` tables + hot-path rules, §5f, §7 Identity and admin. Decisions 7, 13, 15, 23.

## Considerations
- The workspace is the only OIDC client: one redirect URI. Implicit consent lives in the IdP; people see no consent screen.
- Fail open on an unreachable IdP, fail closed on `invalid_grant`; a failed poll changes nothing.
- Never confirm what's behind a name: `not_found` outside a principal's view; the 403 page shows no title.
- The no-cap hop is client-side; framed parts never navigate to `/grant` (no Lax cookie from an opaque-origin subframe), hence the regrant endpoint.
- Pin, never a group. Native step-up makes the IdP's `max_age` irrelevant. One 10-minute window; inward sharing never asks. Unsandboxed origins are never accepted.
- Wrapper-origin assertion lines need the wrapper page, so they are verified in the trusted wrapper bead.
- Every timer takes an injectable clock; e2e advances it through a dev-only endpoint. Parts and grants for e2e come from dev-only subcommands.
- This bead starts as soon as the store lands and runs in parallel with the builds and part host beads (§6a "Identity, in parallel once the schema lands"). `/grant` and the regrant handler mint caps with `pf-caps`, which the part host bead owns: if it hasn't landed, reserve `crates/pf-caps/` through Agent Mail and build it exactly per §2 so both beads share one crate. `grant_flow.spec.ts` asserts the 302 target and the `#pf=` fragment; following the redirect into a served part is the wrapper bead's spec once the content listener is live.
- `/grant`, `/signin` and the regrant handler register their rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead).

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/{oidc_mock,second_provider,sessions,signout,claims_reread,grant_fuzz,webauthn,stepup_guard,admin_guard}.rs`, `crates/pf-policy/tests/{audit,expiry}.rs`, `pf_policy::tests::prop_no_role_above_best_grant`, `rt_matrix_table`, `crates/partifactory/tests/admin_cli.rs`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/identity/{login_roundtrip,group_removal,grant_flow,stepup_workspace}.spec.ts`.
- Logs: `event="session.created"`, `event="directory.refresh" outcome=…`, `event="epoch.bump" reason=…`, `event="policy.decide" outcome="deny"`, `event="grant.decide" mode=…`, `event="stepup.verify"`, `event="admin.break_glass"`; metrics `pf_directory_refresh_total`, `pf_directory_stale`, `pf_epoch_bumps_total`. Never a cap, code, cookie or token.

## Verification gate
- Running build in the harness: Dex sign-in on chromium-desktop and webkit-mobile (and with the second Dex config); a group removal plus clock advance refuses the next part open; `curl -si` of `/grant` shows the cap only after `#pf=`; an outsider gets the 403 page; workspace step-up with the virtual authenticator; break-glass works once.
- CI green on `main`: nextest job and harness e2e job include the tests above.
- Logs: the e2e run asserts `session.created`, `grant.decide`, `directory.refresh`, `stepup.verify`, and no canary cap in any line.
- No regressions in the full e2e suite.
- Evidence on close plus the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Login round trip in e2e against Dex on `parts.pf.test` over TLS, in Chromium and WebKit; the same binary signs in against a second provider config with no code change; sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps the user's minter epoch
- [ ] Sign-in round trip against a discovery-document provider creates a user, a session and the cookie with exactly the attributes above.
- [ ] A second provider config (different issuer, claim names) works with no code change.
- [ ] Sessions slide to 30 days; a no-refresh-token IdP yields 12-hour sessions.
- [ ] Sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps their minter epochs (verified by a cap minted before failing after).
- [ ] `return` cannot redirect off the workspace host (fuzzed).
- [ ] Removing a user from a Dex group fails their next part request after the next re-read (test clock); deleting the user ends the session on `invalid_grant`; with the IdP down, existing sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped
- [ ] With the IdP unreachable for 10 minutes the `idp_unreachable_10m` alert condition is raised and `directory.stale_since` is set; local `pf-*` membership changes bump affected part epochs at once, and a local group not named `pf-*` is rejected by the schema.

title: Agent connections: the token service, the device grant and personal tokens
description:
## Goal
Agents get their own identity, not a shared admin key: one scoped, space-limited, revocable connection per (agent, person), labelled "<agent> for <person>", whose token works on every surface. This bead is the token side of partifactory's own OAuth 2.1 authorization server (issue, refresh rotation, revocation, metadata, 401s), the device grant with its `/device` page, personal tokens and Connected agents. It is built so authorization code after Slice 1 adds an endpoint, not a redesign. The pixel test's agent connects by device code.

## Scope
- [ ] Token store: opaque `pf_at_`/`pf_rt_`/`pf_pat_` + base32 of 160 random bits, stored only as sha256; access 3600 s; single-use refresh rotated in one writer transaction; reuse revokes the family (`invalid_grant`), suspended 24 h after an import; the family ends at the connection's `expires_at`; `POST /oauth/token` (refresh + device-code grants, form in, JSON out) and `POST /oauth/revoke`.
- [ ] Bearer middleware for `/api/*` (and `/mcp` when it lands): every token kind resolves to one `Principal {user_id, connection_id, kind, scopes, spaces, agent_name}`; checks `resource` = `https://parts.<domain>/`, expiry, revocation; any cache is invalidated on revoke. The content listener and `/oauth/*` never accept bearer tokens.
- [ ] Revocation cascade: revoking a connection revokes its refresh family, access tokens and PATs and bumps `minter:conn:<id>`; grants it made stay, listed with "Undo all".
- [ ] Metadata from one struct, listing only mounted endpoints: RFC 9728 protected-resource and RFC 8414 AS metadata (also at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, no `id_token`).
- [ ] 401 contract: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"` plus a JSON `unauthenticated` body naming the ways to get a token; CLI exit 3.
- [ ] `agent_connections` and the shared consent sheet: "This device says it is *Hermes*" (unverified), plain-word scope toggles (share and backends off unless requested), spaces the person may consent (others' spaces need the admin with step-up), lifetime 30 d / 90 d default / 1 y, Allow (passkey when the person has one) / Deny; phone layout.
- [ ] Device grant: built-in public client `part-cli`, `agent_name` (≤ 40) + `software`; `user_code` `XXXX-XXXX` from `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ`, 600 s, interval 5 s, `slow_down` +5 s, single use; `/device` with the big code, coarse origin and age, the stale (> 2 min) and different-network banners, manual entry 5/min/session; signed-out visits return with the code filled; `part login` drives it (terminal QR) and serialises refreshes.
- [ ] Personal tokens from Connected agents (name, scopes, spaces, expiry 30 d default, 1 y max), shown once with the env lines and the `claude mcp add … --header` snippet; never refresh.
- [ ] Connected agents: each connection with scopes, spaces, last used, token type, grants made; Revoke with a 10 s undo toast (undo clears `revoked_at`, never the epoch bump; both audited).

## Plan refs
§3b How agents authenticate, Device grant, Personal agent tokens, Scopes, Revocation cascades; §4a.6 Connecting an agent; §4a.7; §4b Auth per client, Errors; §5c import; §5e `oauth_tokens`, `agent_connections`, `oauth_clients`, `device_codes`; §5f device-connect origin; §7 Agents; decisions 8, 14, 37, 43; docs/agent-contract.md Connecting.

## Considerations
- Opaque, not JWTs: revocation is one row, no key distribution; a DB read per `/api` call is fine off the hot path. Keep an `AuthorizationServer` trait so an IdP with CIMD + RFC 8707 could take over.
- Two concurrent refreshes with one token: the loser triggers family revocation (spec-correct), so clients serialise refreshes.
- One connection per (agent, person) prevents the confused deputy.
- In Slice 1 a person with no passkey approves with their session alone; without an origin source only the age banner fires.
- The `/mcp` lines (401 on `/mcp`, a PAT on `/mcp`) are verified in the MCP, discovery and conformance bead.
- `/oauth/*` and `/device` register their rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead); the 5-per-minute manual code entry is one of them, keyed on the session.

## Tests and logging
- Unit: token store (rotate, reuse, import suspension, expiry, cascade), device codes (test clock), PAT format and bounds, consent rules, property `scope_never_exceeds_person_role`.
- Integration: `revocation_cascade.rs`, `concurrent_refresh.rs`, `bearer_middleware.rs`, `metadata_validate.rs`, `device_two_people.rs` in the oauth crate; `unauthenticated_401.rs`, `pat_parity.rs`, `pat_revoke_next_call.rs` in the api crate; `no_bearer_on_part_host.rs`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/consent_sheet.spec.ts`, `device_grant.spec.ts` (virtual authenticator + mobile WebKit, `part login` subprocess, budget 3), `connected_agents.spec.ts`.
- Logs asserted: `event="device.authorize"`, `event="device.approve"`, `event="token.issue"`, `event="connection.create"`, `event="auth.reject" reason`, `event="cap.verify" outcome="stale_epoch"`; canary tokens never logged.

## Verification gate
- On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness: `part login` is approved on `/device` (mobile WebKit; Chromium with the virtual authenticator) and the token runs `part get`; a PAT from Connected agents works on `/api` and gets 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` right after revoke; the AS metadata lists only mounted endpoints.
- CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest and e2e harness jobs.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="token.issue"` and `event="auth.reject" reason="revoked"`, and no canary token.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, `/device` screenshots at 360 px; `ci_green` and `verified` reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Rotation, reuse revocation, expiry and revocation behave as in Scope.
- [ ] A revoked token fails on the very next call (no stale cache).
- [ ] A token never appears in logs; only its prefix may (`pf_at_…`).
- [ ] Both metadata docs validate against RFC 9728/8414 JSON schemas.
- [ ] Advertised endpoints equal mounted routes (test).
- [ ] Creating a connection outside consentable spaces is refused (`forbidden {space}`), or needs admin step-up.
- [ ] Writes made through a connection record `actor_conn` and render as "<agent> for <person>".
- [ ] Sheet passes the contrast test and the 360 px layout check.
- [ ] `part login` -> code -> approve on phone with a passkey -> token; `slow_down`, `expired_token`, `access_denied` tested; two people pairing Hermes give two connections labelled 'Hermes for <person>'; a household member with no partifactory passkey approves with their session
- [ ] Refresh reuse revokes the family (suspended for 24 h after an import); a token is rejected on part hosts and on `/oauth/*`; every 401 from `/api` carries `WWW-Authenticate` and the JSON body.
- [ ] Revoking a connection revokes its access, refresh and personal tokens and bumps `minter:conn:<id>`; a cap minted through it fails on the next request.
- [ ] Device codes expire at 600 s and are single use; manual code entry is limited to 5 a minute per session; the stale (> 2 min) and different-network banners appear when they should.
- [ ] A PAT is shown once, only its hash is stored, its expiry defaults to 30 days and is capped at 1 year, and it works on `/api` with the same decisions as a device token; revoke from Connected agents (3 interactions, undo toast) gives 401 on the next call.
- [ ] The token service is built as the OAuth AS token side: adding authorization code after Slice 1 needs only new endpoints and metadata fields, not a new token model.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness, `part login` is approved on `/device` (mobile WebKit and Chromium with the virtual authenticator) and the token runs `part get`; a PAT from Connected agents works on `/api` and returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` right after revoke; the AS metadata lists only mounted endpoints.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the token, device and PAT tests (nextest job) and `device_grant.spec.ts`, `connected_agents.spec.ts`, `consent_sheet.spec.ts` (e2e harness job).
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="token.issue"` and `event="auth.reject" reason="revoked"` lines, and no canary token value appears in logs.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, `/device` screenshots with browser versions) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

title: Observability and the e2e harness: logs, metrics, request ids, the ingress contract, Dex + Caddy + pf.test
description:
## Goal
Give partifactory one observability backbone and one production-shaped test bed before any feature lands: redacted JSON logs, Prometheus metrics, `/healthz` and a `/readyz` skeleton, the core of the ingress contract (client address, request ids, the shared rate-limit layer) with the one shipped Caddy config, and the browser e2e harness (Dex, Caddy with an internal-CA cert for `pf.test`, Playwright on Chromium, WebKit and Firefox with mobile emulation, plus the Mobile Safari lane in the iOS Simulator). Every later bead's gate runs in this harness and asserts on these log lines, which is why it comes first.

## Scope
- [ ] Logging (the obs crate): `tracing` JSON to stdout, always on; one access line per request with `request_id, route_class, status, latency_us, principal, outcome` (plus `op`, `surface`, `part_id` when known); the shared field convention `ts, level, target, msg, request_id, route_class, op, surface, part_id, principal, outcome, latency_us` + an `event` name.
- [ ] Redaction by type (`Secret<T>`, `CapToken`, `BearerToken`, `SessionId`, `RefreshToken` print `[redacted]`) plus a pattern layer: `/c/<…>/` -> `/c/[cap]/`, `pf_at_|pf_rt_|pf_pat_` tokens redacted, `Authorization`/`Cookie`/`Set-Cookie` never recorded, `Location` values with `#pf=` stripped. Runtime log-level reload handle.
- [ ] Metrics on `:9090/metrics` behind `PF_METRICS_TOKEN` (401 otherwise): RED per route class (`workspace_ui, api, mcp, oauth, grant, content_entry, content_blob, rt, wrapper, blob_host, chrome_api, ops`) and per op via `record_op(op, surface, outcome, dur)`; skeleton gauges later beads fill, incl. `pf_nonpart_host_hits_total` and `pf_rate_limited_total`. No part names, principals or request ids as labels.
- [ ] `/healthz` and a `/readyz` check registry: DB writable, blob store OK, disk headroom > 5 %; `degraded` rows (IdP, directory poll, backup freshness) never cause 503; `importing` field reserved.
- [ ] Ingress contract core: `ClientAddr` layer on both public listeners (header from `[ingress] client_ip_header` trusted only from `trusted_proxies`; right-most untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` hop); request-id layer (`request_id_header` value if trusted, printable and ≤ 128 chars, else generated), echoed as a response header and shown on a minimal error page.
- [ ] The shared rate-limit layer (§5d, on by default): a `governor` tower layer keyed on the trusted client address, and on the principal once a later layer attaches one, with a route table `{route_class, key, limit, window}` that later beads register their routes in (`/grant`, `/oauth/*`, `/device`, `/l/*`, `/_rt` reads and writes, `/api`, `/mcp`, `part_check`); 429 + `Retry-After`, `event="ratelimit.trip" route_class key_kind`, `pf_rate_limited_total{route_class}`; a safe default that only `[unsafe] rate_limits = "off"` disables. Nothing is registered yet except a self-test route.
- [ ] `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` (the one Caddy config in the repo: two site blocks by Host, wildcard cert, `X-Forwarded-For`, SSE flush, 8 MiB bodies, 60 s streams, serves the maintenance page when the origin is down), `deploy/proxy/maintenance.html` (static `503 · DOWN FOR MAINTENANCE`, inlined CSS), and `deploy/proxy/smoke.sh`.
- [ ] `tests/e2e/harness/`: Dex (static users/groups matching the fixture identities, refresh tokens and groups claim on, a second config for the second-provider test), Caddy mounting the shipped Caddyfile with test cert paths, a per-run internal CA trusted by the browsers (never `--ignore-certificate-errors`), host resolution (Chromium `--host-resolver-rules`, WebKit and Firefox via `/etc/hosts` or dnsmasq), Playwright projects `chromium-desktop` (virtual WebAuthn authenticator), `chromium-mobile` (phone viewport, touch, virtual authenticator), `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop`, partifactory started from compose with `_FILE` secrets.
- [ ] The iOS Simulator lane, `tests/device/ios-sim.sh`: boots a device on the installed iOS runtime (`xcrun simctl boot`), trusts the harness CA (`simctl keychain add-root-cert`), resolves `*.pf.test` through the Mac's `/etc/hosts`, opens a self-reporting page with `simctl openurl`, waits for the page's POST to the harness collector, takes `simctl io screenshot`, and writes `target/e2e-logs/ios-sim/<spec>/`. It runs locally on the Mac (or a macOS runner if one exists) and is never a required CI check: beads whose gate names it attach its output to their `verified` report.
- [ ] Click-budget helper; per-test artifacts (server JSONL, trace, screenshots, HAR) under `target/e2e-logs/<test-name>/`; failing request ids printed.

## Plan refs
§5d Logs, Metrics, Health and alerting, Abuse prevention (rate limits); §3 Topology (ops listener, the ingress contract, hostnames); §2 Serving (leaked URLs: logs redact `/c/<…>/`); §5f the portability lane; §3a and §4a.7 click budgets; §4a.6 error pages; §7 Operations; Slice 1 definition of done item 1.

## Considerations
- `/readyz` never depends on the IdP: tying readiness to it would roll back deploys and show the maintenance page exactly when the product is fine.
- `:9090` is never routed through the ingress and still needs the token: local network is not trusted. The Caddyfile must not expose it.
- Fail closed on spoofing: a header from an untrusted peer is ignored entirely, not partially used. Rate limits key on that vetted address, otherwise everyone shares one bucket or anyone spoofs out of theirs.
- The rate-limit layer lives here so every later surface registers into one table instead of hand-rolling its own; the public-links bead owns the guest limits and the table-driven test across every registered route.
- The harness is vendor-free by construction; the later portability lane reuses it as is.
- The harness self-test needs no sign-in code: a dev-only stub route sets a `__Host-` test cookie. The Dex sign-in round trip is the identity bead's check.
- Real phones never block anything (the admin's rule): phones are Playwright's mobile projects and the iOS Simulator. The simulator shares the Mac's network and keychain tooling, so no certificate-error flags; the real-device checks are the non-blocking human-checks bead.

## Tests and logging
- `pf_obs::redact::tests::*` (unit + proptest: random caps and tokens in arbitrary strings never survive); obs crate tests `canary_logs.rs::canary_values_never_logged` (log kept at `target/test-logs/` on failure) and `metrics_auth.rs`; `crates/partifactory/tests/health.rs` (`readyz_reports_failing_check`, `readyz_ignores_degraded`); `request_id_from_trusted_header`, `log_level_runtime_reload`.
- `pf_serve::ingress::tests::{xff_rightmost_untrusted, untrusted_peer_header_ignored, request_id_sanitised_or_generated}`; `crates/pf-serve/tests/ingress_contract.rs` asserts `event="http.request"` with `client_ip` and `request_id`; `crates/pf-serve/tests/ratelimit_layer.rs` (a registered self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1, keyed per client address; `event="ratelimit.trip"` logged; `pf_rate_limited_total` increments).
- `tests/e2e/harness/self_test.spec.ts` (all four Playwright projects), `tests/e2e/harness/second_provider.spec.ts`, `tests/e2e/proxy_smoke.spec.ts` (Host routing, 60 s SSE hold, 8 MiB POST, maintenance page with the upstream stopped); `tests/device/ios-sim.sh self-test` opens the self-test page in the simulator and records its post and screenshot.

## Verification gate
- In the harness: `self_test.spec.ts` passes on `chromium-desktop`, `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` against `https://parts.pf.test` with a valid TLS chain; `proxy_smoke.spec.ts` holds SSE 60 s through Caddy, accepts 8 MiB, rejects 8 MiB + 1, and shows the maintenance page with the origin stopped; `tests/device/ios-sim.sh self-test` on the Mac records the simulator's post and screenshot (attached to `verified`).
- On the running binary: `curl -s :9090/metrics` -> 401, with the token -> 200 with `pf_http_requests_total{route_class=...}`; a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` from an untrusted peer is ignored in the access line; the rate-limit self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1.
- CI green on `main` with the nextest job and a new `e2e` harness job; the harness job uploads `target/e2e-logs/` on failure.
- Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="http.request"` lines carrying `request_id` and `client_ip`, and one `event="ratelimit.trip"` from the self-test route.
- No regressions; evidence on close (SHAs, CI run ids, the smoke output, browser, simulator runtime and Caddy versions) with `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Canary token/cap/content values never appear in logs under the test suite; /metrics exposes RED metrics per route class and op, and returns 401 without the token
- [ ] The Caddy config passes a smoke test (routing by Host, SSE survives 60 s, 8 MiB body); a spoofed client-IP header from an untrusted address is ignored; the request id appears in logs and error pages
- [ ] `harness/self_test.spec.ts` passes on `chromium-desktop` and `webkit-mobile` over TLS at `https://parts.pf.test` (`login_roundtrip` is the identity bead's closing check and needs the OIDC client as well).
- [ ] A virtual authenticator can be added in Chromium tests (smoke assertion; used by the step-up, share-sheet and pixel tests).
- [ ] A test part host `<name>-part.pf.test` resolves in both browsers.
- [ ] Failing tests leave server JSONL, trace, screenshots and HAR under `target/e2e-logs/<test-name>/`.
- [ ] The click-budget helper fails a test when a scripted path exceeds its budget.
- [ ] Harness runs with no external network access other than pulling images.
- [ ] `/healthz` returns 200; `/readyz` returns 503 naming the failing check (DB, blobs or disk headroom), and a registered degraded check never causes 503.
- [ ] Every request produces exactly one JSON access line with `request_id`, `route_class`, `status`, `latency_us`, `principal` (or null) and `outcome`, and the log level changes at runtime without a restart.
- [ ] `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` is the only Caddy config in the repo, and the harness mounts it with only the cert paths overridden.
- [ ] `chromium-mobile` (phone viewport, touch, virtual authenticator) and `firefox-desktop` Playwright projects exist beside `chromium-desktop` and `webkit-mobile`, and `self_test.spec.ts` passes on all four; the part host resolves in Firefox too.
- [ ] `tests/device/ios-sim.sh` boots an iOS Simulator device, trusts the harness CA in its keychain, opens a self-reporting page on `https://parts.pf.test` with `simctl openurl`, collects the page's POST and a screenshot under `target/e2e-logs/ios-sim/`, and exits non-zero when the post never arrives; it is documented as a local lane whose output is attached to `verified` reports, never a required CI check.
- [ ] A `governor` rate-limit layer keyed on the trusted client address (and on the principal once one is attached) exists with a route table later beads register into; a self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1, logs `event="ratelimit.trip"`, increments `pf_rate_limited_total`, and switching the layer off without `[unsafe] rate_limits = "off"` fails `config check`.
- [ ] GATE: In the harness, `self_test.spec.ts` (all four Playwright projects) and `proxy_smoke.spec.ts` pass on the binary built from `main`; `tests/device/ios-sim.sh self-test` on the Mac records the simulator's post and screenshot; browser, simulator runtime and Caddy versions recorded.
- [ ] GATE: On the running binary, `curl :9090/metrics` gives 401 without the token and 200 with `pf_http_requests_total{route_class=...}` with it; a spoofed client-IP header from an untrusted peer is ignored in the access line; the rate-limit self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the nextest job and the new `e2e` harness job, which keeps `target/e2e-logs/` as an artifact on failure.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="http.request"` lines with `request_id` and `client_ip` and one `event="ratelimit.trip"` from the self-test route, and the canary test finds no canary value.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions; closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run ids, smoke output, the simulator lane output) and `ci_green` + `verified` gate reports.

title: Store core: SQLite, schema v1, blobs, versions, names, spaces and the part service
description:
## Goal
The storage foundation every later bead writes into: SQLite with one serialising writer, schema v1 exactly as the plan's data model, the content-addressed blob store, immutable versions, names, personal spaces and the part service, with idempotent writes. It also defines the provider-neutral identity traits and a static fixture directory, so every test signs in without a network. Constraints live in the database, so later beads can trust their invariants.

## Scope
- [ ] `pf-db`: rusqlite (bundled, FTS5), WAL, `foreign_keys=ON`, `synchronous=FULL` on the one writer task, `query_only` read pool, embedded forward-only migrations with a sha check, a second `Db` for `insights.db`, `temp_db()` for tests.
- [ ] Schema v1: `0001_schema_v1.sql` (main DDL verbatim, incl. `build_deps`, `advisories`, backend tables, `parts_fts` without triggers) and `insights/0001_insights_v1.sql`; `schema_test` with helpers and a golden snapshot.
- [ ] `pf-blobs`: `BlobStore` + local `/data/blobs/ab/cd/<sha256>`; temp -> fsync -> verify -> rename; idempotent concurrent puts; verify-on-read; stale-temp sweep; `DiskBudget` hook (`storage_full` at 95 %).
- [ ] Versions: JCS (RFC 8785) manifest whose hash is the version id; `commit_version` in the writer; head/live with `set_live_if_newer`; v0 placeholder; path rules.
- [ ] Names: `[a-z0-9-]` 1-58, `blobs` reserved in code, `[names] reserved`, every name ever used reserved forever, `derive(title)`, deterministic ranked alternatives.
- [ ] Spaces: personal space per person, default space for a person or their agent, live-inherited space grants (`max(part, space)`), `effective_quota`, `move_part` bumps the epoch.
- [ ] Part service: create (all `part_create` fields, `check_only`, fork, `expires_in`, `snapshots`), the shared idempotency layer, get (version, <= 32 KiB content, `file`/`range`, history, diff), delete to the 30-day bin, undelete, restore as append, `expire_due_parts`.
- [ ] `pf-auth`: `Authn`, `Directory`, placeholder `Provisioner`; `StaticDirectory` from `tests/fixtures/identity.toml` (admin, two household members, an outsider, a disabled user; three groups), `invalid_grant`/`Unreachable` switches, `TestSession::sign_in`.
- [ ] Dev-only subcommands (`dev` feature, never in release): `partifactory dev put|get|history|diff|delete|undelete|restore|fork|sign-in`, so the gate drives the running binary before the HTTP API exists.

## Plan refs
§2 The core idea, §3a Three layers and Spaces, §3d Creation contract, Idempotent, Durable when acknowledged, Linearisable writes, §3e Versions and the bin, §4 Names, §5d Migrations, §5e Data model, §5h; docs/agent-contract.md `part_create`, `part_get`, Rules 1 and 7.

## Considerations
- One writer makes `n` gap-free, rebase safe and "acknowledged = survives a power cut". No save waits on a backup target.
- Migrations run before the health-gated switch and must work with the previous binary; never edit `0001` once released. Bundled SQLite >= 3.45; forward `REFERENCES` are fine.
- STRICT tables, prefixed ULID ids, unix-ms times, secrets only as sha256, JSON `json_valid`. No FTS triggers (search fills `parts_fts` in code). Backend tables exist now so P2a needs no disruptive migration.
- The blob store is filesystem-only; callers write `blobs` rows in their writer transaction. Shared vs part class belongs to the reference.
- The manifest includes `part_id`, `parent` and `n`: identical files in two parts never share an id. Every version is kept.
- Names are not secret; reserve forever because renames 301 forever. Never copy space grants onto parts. Slice 1 has personal spaces only.

**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Finish P2, "agents + the household loop", on top of what Slice 1 shipped (tokens, device code, MCP, part_edit, part_check, shared data, contribute links). This epic adds what makes the loop daily: browser OAuth for MCP clients, comments for the agent, the event feed, inward sharing by agents, live reload, Jig, the source editor, renames, the Insights and debugging pages, and the Hermes skill. P2's Done-when (beyond the pixel test, which is Slice 1's exit) is reached here.

## Scope
- [ ] OAuth authorization code: `/oauth/authorize` with PKCE S256 only, `iss` (RFC 9207), `resource` = the workspace origin (RFC 8707); CIMD clients (fetched through the mirror egress guard), DCR (rate-limited, inert until consent, purged after 1 h), manual clients with a secret (admin area, step-up); consent sheet shows the redirect host and warns on a localhost CIMD redirect; joins conformance as the third auth kind.
- [ ] Leases (`part_edit {claim}`): part scope by default, file or block, TTL ≤ 10 min, checked inside the writer with rebase, released on commit or expiry; the person can always override (agents never force).
- [ ] Block ids for markdown: `.pf/blocks.json` in the manifest, three-pass carry-over (hash LCS, same-kind Jaccard ≥ 0.5, fresh id), block ops, `pf:pending` placeholders.
- [ ] Read path extras: agent notes (`part_notes`, ≤ 16 KiB, no new version), outline with symbols for large parts, `render: "text"`, `part_find` (FTS5 search from the rest of P1) with filters and "recent by me / this agent".
- [ ] Comments (`part_comments` + `/_rt comments.*`): threads, anchors, `to_agent`, resolve/reopen, `provenance`, `contains_untrusted`, MCP `<untrusted_content>` wrapper; link-viewer comments only with the per-part opt-in; the comments rail in the wrapper with "For the agent"; Details "Send to agent".
- [ ] Events for agents: `part_watch` long-poll (25 s default, 50 s max), `GET /api/v1/events` SSE with `Last-Event-ID` and 25 s heartbeat, `cursor_expired` after 30 days, HMAC-signed webhooks (config-only targets, retried).
- [ ] Agent sharing with `share:household`: inward grants and moves only, labelled "Hermes shared this", one-tap undo, "Undo all" on revoke; no outward path on any surface.
- [ ] The remaining `part_link_for` actions: `group`, `everyone`, `admin` (`invite` lands with P2b, `lan` with P2a).
- [ ] Jig: `jig.css` shared blob, `--jig-*` tokens, four presets, `@partifactory/jig`, Jig as a part in `system`, `design_system` op + contract section; markdown, text and code shells move from `pf-shell.css` to Jig.
- [ ] The workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6 (vendored shared blob), server drafts per (person, part), `d`-claim preview caps, diff3 merge with Resolve (Keep mine / Keep theirs / Edit), lease notice.
- [ ] Live reload: `pf:version` from the wrapper (or the prelude when standalone); silent reload, or a toast when personal state is unsaved.
- [ ] Renames: admin-confirmed with step-up, old host 301s forever with the query stripped, old name reserved, old caps die.
- [ ] Insights pages (Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds) over the Insights store; the debugging UI (trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab with denying decisions, per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail).
- [ ] Workspace activity feed and Shared with me.
- [ ] The Hermes skill: per-person pairing by device code, `part_check` before posting, comment relay, deep links.

## Plan refs
§3b (OAuth 2.1, agent sharing, revocation cascades), §3c, §3d (leases, long documents), §3e, §4 (ops table, events, no notifications), §4a.6 and §4a.7 (comments, editor, budgets), §4a.8 Jig, §4b, §4c, §5g, §6 P2, §6a "The rest of P2", decisions 13, 34, 37.

## Considerations
- Decision 37: auth code is after Slice 1; the slice's token service is already the AS token side, so this adds an endpoint, not a redesign. `share:household` is off by default for CIMD, DCR and manual clients; `backends:deploy` is off for every client.
- CIMD and mirror-on-build share one egress guard: https only, private/loopback/link-local refused after DNS resolution, ≤ 5 KiB, 3 s, no redirects.
- No CRDTs. Block ids live in the manifest so identity versions with content; anchors and lease refs hold ids as text, no FK.
- Comment bodies are content and never logged (the no-content fuzz test). "Untrusted for agents" is a reading aid shown to the owner.
- No approval queues: a deep link grants nothing and stores nothing pending; there is no request table (schema test).
- Jig must never look like the chrome (a part must never pass for the workspace); old parts keep loading their recorded `jig.css` hash.
- Insights and debug pages are admin-only. Non-admins get 403 (§7: only the pinned subject reaches admin), which supersedes an older 404 line. Guests appear only as counts; the per-agent page shows argument keys and sizes, never values. "Deep links acted on" = the matching share-sheet action by the admin on the same part within 7 days.
- Live reload coalesces events within 500 ms. partifactory never messages Telegram; Hermes treats `<untrusted_content>` as data.

## Order inside the phase
From §6a: OAuth authorization code; comments, leases, block ids, notes and `part_find` (after search in the rest of P1); `part_watch` and webhooks → the source editor; agent sharing → the Hermes skill; Jig; live reload; renames; the Insights pages (after the Insights store, traces and the log pipeline in the rest of P1) → the debugging UI; the remaining deep links.

title: Public links and guests: admin-only links, Can view and Can contribute, part_link_for, guest limits, rate limits and freeze
description:
## Goal
Public links are the one way a part leaves the house, so only the admin makes them: unlisted, `noindex`, revocable, no expiry by default, counted. A **Can contribute** link turns each tab into a guest who writes the part's shared data and nothing else. This is how a signed-out phone paints the pixel board while the admin can roll back, reset or freeze, and how an agent hands its person the one tap it may not take itself (`part_link_for`).

## Scope
- [ ] `public_links` lifecycle: session-only handlers, admin + fresh step-up, live version required; 128-bit token stored as sha256; expiry Never / 1 / 7 / 30 days; audited.
- [ ] `GET /l/<token>` on the part host: the wrapper in public mode with the content-free public card and a JS hop; no cap, no target URL, no `<meta refresh>`, byte-identical for every UA. `POST /l/<token>/go` mints the `link:<id>` cap and is what counts an open.
- [ ] Revoke (minter epoch bump, then plain 404), expiry (`410 · LINK EXPIRED`), the "Revoke all public links" kill switch (audited). `/p/<name>` on the workspace only 302s to the part host, the same for unknown names.
- [ ] Guests: `go` on a contribute link adds `dw` and a random guest id `g` ("Guest 4f2a"); with `dw`, shared `storage.*` reads and writes; without it, shared writes are `forbidden_view_only`; every non-data `/_rt` op and any `/api` or `/mcp` request is 403; writes labelled `guest:<link>:<g>`.
- [ ] Switching to Can contribute takes a `reason: contribute` snapshot (outside `keep`) and sets `shared_data_writers` to `viewers`; Freeze sets view mode and bumps the link's minter epoch; `editors` while a contribute link is active freezes it. Roll back / Reset use the snapshot engine.
- [ ] Rate limits on the shared `governor` layer from the observability bead: register `/l/*`, the per-guest (60/min) and per-IP (300/min) `/_rt` write rows and the 600/min read row; the table-driven test over every registered route (`/grant`, `/oauth/*`, `/device`, `/l/*`, `/_rt`, `/api`, `/mcp`, `part_check`) at threshold + 1 with 429 + `Retry-After`; pre-auth body caps (§5d) before any auth or DB work.
- [ ] Share sheet, Slice 1 rungs, inside the wrapper: the ladder (inward rungs disabled), the amber admin-only public rung, live sentence, mode, expiry, Copy, open count, Revoke with a 10 s undo toast, Roll back / Reset / Freeze, "Data: view only", in-sheet step-up, guest edit counts.
- [ ] `part_link_for {name, action: public_link | contribute}` -> `{action, url, who: "admin"}`; the sheet opens pre-filled from `#share=public` / `#share=contribute`, the fragment survives the `/grant` hop, nothing is saved until confirmed; no request table exists.

## Plan refs
§2 public links; §3a audience ladder, Can contribute, role x runtime matrix, step-up; §4 `part_link_for`, no queues; §4a.6-4a.7; §5d abuse prevention; §5e `public_links`; §7 Links, Guests, Operations; decisions 12, 31, 34; agent contract `part_link_for`, Rules 4-5.

## Considerations
- Public links are DB tokens, not HMAC caps: key rotation never touches them. Counting on the `go` POST keeps unfurlers from inflating counts.
- The guest id is a signed claim in the link cap: per tab, no cookie; a forged `g` fails the MAC and looks like not found (404).
- A guest never has more than a signed-in viewer, hence the `editors` -> freeze coupling. Freeze bumps the link's minter epoch, not the part epoch, so people's caps stay valid.
- Key limits on the client IP only from trusted proxies (ingress contract), else everyone shares one bucket or spoofs. The layer itself ships with the observability bead; this bead adds the link and guest rows and proves the whole table.
- The guest half also runs from Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`); real phones never block anything.
- Agent-token refusal on every surface needs agent connections and MCP; it is verified in the MCP, discovery and conformance bead.

## Tests and logging
- Integration: `public_link_lifecycle.rs`, `guest_wall.rs`, `guest_caps.rs` + proptest `guest_cap_never_grants_non_data`, `contribute_switch.rs`, `rate_limits.rs` (route x key x threshold, test clock), `preauth_body_caps.rs` (zero DB queries), `part_link_for.rs`, `schema_no_queue.rs`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/share_sheet_public.spec.ts`, `share_sheet_contribute.spec.ts`, `contribute_link.spec.ts`, `deep_link_share.spec.ts`, with the click-budget counter and light/dark/360 px snapshots.
- Logs asserted: `event="link.create|link.go|link.revoke"` with `outcome`, `event="stepup.verify"`, `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:<id>"`, `event="rt.op" principal="guest:..." outcome="forbidden"`, `event="ratelimit.trip"`; metric `pf_rate_limited_total`; never a cap or token.

## Verification gate
- Harness, binary from `main`: the admin on chromium-desktop (virtual authenticator) makes a Can-contribute link in 4 interactions + 1 biometric; a signed-out webkit-mobile guest opens it and paints, and the admin's tab shows it; the admin freezes and the guest's next write is refused; revoke gives 404.
- `curl` of `/l/<token>` with a bot and a browser UA gives byte-identical HTML with no cap; a guest cap gets 403 on `comments.*` and `/api`; the 61st guest write in a minute gets 429.
- `part_link_for {action: "contribute"}` from the CLI returns the `#share=contribute` URL, which opens the pre-filled rung after sign-in.
- CI green on `main`: these tests in the nextest job, the specs in the e2e harness job.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="link.go"`, `event="epoch.bump"` and `event="ratelimit.trip"`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Close with evidence: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, screenshot and trace paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A fresh browser with no session opens `/l/<token>` and sees the part. `open_count` increments by exactly 1 per go-hop.
- [ ] After revoke, the next `/l/` and the next `/c/` request with the link cap return 404 within seconds.
- [ ] The `/l/` HTML contains no cap, no hop-target URL and no `<meta refresh>`, and is identical across UAs.
- [ ] The kill switch revokes all and writes audit rows.

title: Health, export and import: the Health page, /readyz, nightly export, import with the boot-epoch bump, the regrant helper
description:
## Goal
One place where the admin sees whether the box is healthy, and a `/data` that restores: an hourly consistent DB copy, a nightly `partifactory export` with nothing configured, and `partifactory import` that brings it back anywhere and kills every cap minted before it. The server is left alone for years, so the backup must exist before anyone asks; **no save ever waits on a backup target**.

## Scope
- [ ] `/readyz` on the ops listener (`:9090`): DB writable (write through the single writer), blob store OK (probe put/has/get), disk headroom > 5 %, `importing=true` → 503; body `{ready, checks, degraded}`. IdP reachability, directory staleness and backup freshness are **degraded rows, never readiness**. One `HealthCheck` trait shared by `/readyz`, the page, later `doctor` and the alert webhook.
- [ ] Admin Health page `/admin/health` (admin pin, no step-up to read): checks, degraded rows, backup layers (host snapshots on/off/unknown; newest export age, size, same-disk flag), disk use by biggest spaces and parts, reserved rows for the disk budget and store caps (filled by the retention bead), quota hits, 5xx spikes, version, last drill, break-glass uses, safe defaults switched off, runtime log level (audited). Chips are icon + words.
- [ ] Hourly `VACUUM INTO backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite.tmp` → `integrity_check` → fsync → rename; failure keeps the previous copy and raises staleness.
- [ ] `partifactory export` → `partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst`: `MANIFEST.json` with a sha256 per entry, consistent `db.sqlite`, every referenced blob (the blob-GC mark function), `--parts-only` (no access records, tokens or people), `--encrypt` (age recipient), `--include-insights`, `--include-secrets` (needs `--encrypt`). Temp file, fsync, rename.
- [ ] Nightly export on by default to `/data/exports`, keep 7 (`backup.export_schedule|export_dir|export_keep`); off needs `[unsafe]`; newest export time/size in `kv` and metrics; same-filesystem detection by `st_dev`.
- [ ] `partifactory import <file>`: verify every entry before writing anything, load `db.sqlite` + forward migrations, blobs temp → fsync → rename, **bump the boot epoch**, serve with `importing=true` until blobs verify; `--force` moves the old DB aside; records `kv.import_at` (the token service suspends refresh-reuse detection for 24 h after it). Parts-only import recreates history, author labels and timestamps (placeholder users), with no grants, tokens or sessions.
- [ ] `partifactory import regrant --plan` / `--apply plan.json`: proposes grants by stored audience names (groups by name, people by username or email); the one-screen UI comes later.

## Plan refs
§5c Backups, recovery and self-provisioning, §5d Health and alerting, §5h, §4a.6 Admin Health, §2 Keys (boot-epoch floor), §3a (fail open on an unreachable IdP); Slice 1 definition of done items 5 and 6; decision 17.

## Considerations
- Readiness never depends on the IdP, or an IdP outage would roll back deploys and show the maintenance page while the product works. Probes < 50 ms.
- `/data` + export, not git, Litestream or a streaming sink (round 2; Litestream v0.5 dropped age). `VACUUM INTO` reads a WAL snapshot without blocking the writer. Host rsync-style copies must take the hourly file, never the live `.db`.
- age to a public recipient: the box never holds the identity; it lives offline with the site config.
- An export on the same disk as `/data` is amber, never green; no export in 48 h is amber too.
- The boot-epoch bump is what makes restoring an old DB safe; cost: one silent re-grant per open tab.
- Every condition the later alert webhook mirrors is already a Health row (budget 80 %, store 80 % of cap, no export 48 h, crash-loops, IdP down 10 min).
- Moved to the Shipping bead: the drill line (needs the image) and the refresh-reuse-after-import line (needs the token service deployed); this bead still records `kv.import_at`.

## Tests and logging
- `pf_obs::health::tests::*`, `crates/partifactory/tests/health_page.rs::rows_cover_alert_conditions`, `idp_down_readyz_200_degraded_row` (Dex stopped).
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/{export_during_burst.rs, nightly_default.rs, roundtrip.rs::full_export_import_identical, roundtrip.rs::old_caps_dead_after_import, parts_only_import.rs}`; `tests/e2e/health_page.spec.ts`.
- Logs asserted: `event="health.check" name="idp" outcome="degraded"`, `event="backup.copy"`, `event="export.finished" outcome="ok" entries=<n> bytes=<b>`, `event="import.verify"`, `event="import.boot_epoch_bump" new_floor=<n>`, `event="import.finished"`, `event="cap.verify" outcome="stale_boot"`. Metrics `pf_ready`, `pf_backup_copy_last_success_timestamp_seconds`, newest export age.

## Verification gate
1. Binary from `main` in the e2e harness: the admin opens `https://parts.pf.test/admin/health` and sees readiness, backup and disk rows; with Dex stopped `curl :9090/readyz` is 200 with a degraded IdP row. A test-clock nightly export imported into a fresh data dir brings back every part, version, data doc and snapshot; a pre-export cap gets 302/401 and a fresh `/grant` works.
2. CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest job, `health_page.spec.ts` in the e2e job.
3. The run asserts `event="import.boot_epoch_bump"` and `event="export.finished" outcome="ok"`.
4. The full e2e suite, every earlier gate included, still passes.
5. Close with SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts and the Health screenshot path; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded via `br gate report`.

title: P2a Backends: the runner, builds, lifecycle, routing, data and secrets, the backend contract and the backend pixel test
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
A part becomes a page plus, optionally, containers (decision 28): a Dockerfile, a registry image or an uploaded image in a small compose subset, built by the server, health-gated per version, routed under the cap with a signed identity header, and walled off from the LAN. Only a runner sidecar holds the Docker/Podman Engine API.

## Scope
- [ ] **Runner spike** (`docs/spikes/runner.md`, `docs/spikes/runner/run.sh docker|podman`): rootless BuildKit in a container; drop rules in `DOCKER-USER` and a runner-owned nftables table (netavark); the runner's privileges (`NET_ADMIN` + host netns); `postgres` under the template; a per-volume disk limit; the pinned SBOM scanner (Syft default, Trivy alternative).
- [ ] **The runner**: `partifactory runner` (`bollard`), fixed API `build/deploy/start/stop/logs/stats/prune` with `PF_RUNNER_KEY`, containers only from one hardened template; behind the `backends` profile in `deploy/compose.yaml`, the only service mounting the socket.
- [ ] **Networks**: a bridge network per part; egress on and metered; private, CGNAT, link-local, ULA, `[backends] household_subnets`, host and sibling ranges dropped for containers and builds; allowlist accept rules; denied attempts counted; `docs/backends-network.md`; a `doctor` check.
- [ ] **Sources and builds**: the closed compose subset; op-time allowlist scan of `image:` and Dockerfile `FROM`; rootless BuildKit (10 min, 2 CPU / 4 GiB, 10 GiB LRU cache); digests pinned; `POST /api/v1/images` + `part put --image`; build records `target=backend`.
- [ ] **Backend SBOMs and base images (§3h)**: an image SBOM per build from the pinned scanner (`builds.sbom_hash`, 5 MiB cap); a nightly base-image tag re-resolve (`base_image_checks`). Matching is the advisories epic's.
- [ ] **Lifecycle**: a container set per live version; 60 s health gate; 30 s drain; scale to zero (10 s hold, 15 min idle), `always_on`, cron; crash-loop detection (5 in 10 min); `restore: n` starts version n's images.
- [ ] **Routing**: `/c/<cap>/api/*` with the content verifier and role matrix; strip cap, `Cookie`, `pf_` tokens, incoming `X-PF-*`; add `X-PF-Identity` (HS256, per-part HKDF key, 60 s) and `X-PF-Request-Id`; HTTP, WebSocket, SSE.
- [ ] **Data, secrets, permissions**: volumes (`/data/parts/<id>/vol/<svc>`, 1 GiB) exported via hook or stop-copy-start; write-only secrets; `backends:deploy` (off by default); quotas; `part_edit {backend}`, `part_get {backend: true}`; LAN allowlist (admin, step-up) and `part_link_for {action: "lan"}`.
- [ ] **The backend contract** in `docs/agent-contract.md`, in the change that ships backends, with the identity verifier snippet.
- [ ] **Observability and retention**: log rings (50 MiB, 7 days), restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN on the Backends page and Debug tab; image pruning (live + previous 2), cache prune, retention-test rows.
- [ ] **The §7 Backends suite** on Docker and Podman, and **`communal_pixel_editor_backend`**.

## Plan refs
§3f, §3g, §3h layer 3, §5e, §5g, §5h, §6 P2a, §6a, §7 Backends, decisions 28, 29, 34, 51.

## Considerations
- **Rollback is best effort; a backend's data is its own agent's business (decision 51).** Volumes belong to the part and every version shares them; a restore brings back code only. partifactory guarantees two things: the code is exactly what it was built from, and a version never goes live unless its health check passes (else `backend_unhealthy`, and the current set keeps serving). It runs no migrations, down-migrations or data rollbacks. Data snapshots never cover volumes; folder backups and exports do. Tests say so, so nobody "fixes" it into data rollback.
- **The backend contract**: migrate forward with additive changes; versions overlap during the 30 s drain (and a restored version meets the newest data), so read from storage per request and lock writes; back up before a non-additive change (e.g. `pg_dump` into the volume) and say so in the edit message; exit promptly on SIGTERM.
- The template is a code constant the runner enforces itself (UID ≥ 10000, no socket, host network, devices or extra mounts; optional `runsc`).
- The health wait runs outside the single writer; only the live flip commits inside it (§3d).
- Revocation is checked before any byte reaches the backend. Backend log text is untrusted: escaped, admin-only.
- Never prune an image a running set uses; older restores rebuild, re-pull by digest, or report the tarball is needed.
- Pin `postgres:<major>` by digest, mirrored into a local CI registry; fall back to a tiny `FROM postgres` Dockerfile if the template breaks it.
- Without a runner, backend parts fail with `backends_unavailable` (503); frontends are unaffected.

## Order inside the phase
Runner spike → runner (after the Slice 1 deliverable) → backend builds → lifecycle → routing (after Can-contribute links; request ids exist from the observability bead, their trace propagation from the rest of P1) and data, secrets and permissions → the backend security suite and `communal_pixel_editor_backend`. SBOMs and base-image checks come with the runner. The backend Insights pages need the P2 Insights UI.

## Verification gate
- `communal_pixel_editor_backend` passes on the binary built from `main` in the compose deployment, on Docker and Podman and in the portability lane: one `part_edit` adds a Postgres leaderboard, guests' counts show live, a restore brings back the previous code with volume rows intact, and the backend reaches a public canary but not the LAN canary.
- CI green on `main` with the Docker and Podman backend jobs and the §7 Backends suite.
- Logs checked: `event="runner.refused"`, `event="runner.lan_denied"`, `event="backend.set"`, `event="backend.proxy"`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, every Slice 1 gate and `communal_pixel_editor` still pass.
- Every resulting bead closes with evidence and the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.

title: Shared data and live events: window.storage over /_rt, data.changed, snapshots and part_data
description:
## Goal
Give a part shared state that everyone allowed can write, with open pages repainting live when someone else writes, and a one-action undo for bad writes. `window.storage` (Claude's artifact API, plus paging and `getMany`) runs over `/_rt`; one append-only `events` log feeds `/_rt/events` SSE; per-part data snapshots are on by default; agents read, write and roll back the same documents with `part_data`. This is the pixel board's data layer, on the Slice 1 critical path.

## Scope
- [ ] `/_rt` `storage.get/getMany/set/delete/list` over `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1` (text/plain JSON, never a preflight): personal scope keyed by the cap's person (link viewers and guests have none: memory only), shared scope `owner = ''` in `data_docs`, collection `__storage`, key = `doc_id`.
- [ ] Authorisation from the cap's role, `dw` claim and `parts.shared_data_writers` (`viewers` default; `editors` = "Data: view only"): `forbidden_view_only` (403) for view/comment grantees on an `editors` part and for a Can-view link always. Expose the freeze hook for a contribute link when a part goes `editors`.
- [ ] The §3a limits with exact codes (`invalid_input`, `too_large`, `quota_exceeded {kind}`, `rate_limited` + `retry_after`, `storage_full`); a `getMany` or `list` page counts as one read. Guest/IP write limits plug in from the public-links bead.
- [ ] Prelude `window.storage` with Claude's exact signatures (the options object may stand in for `shared`), `PfError {code, message, retryable, retry_after?}` rejections, and `partifactory.on("data.changed", fn)` over one shared `EventSource`, self-echo suppressed by a per-tab writer id, reconnect with backoff through the regrant path.
- [ ] `events` table + in-memory per-part broadcast: append inside the writer transaction, publish after commit, 30-day retention; `GET /c/<cap>/_rt/events` cap-authenticated like `/_rt/v1`, 25 s heartbeat, `pf:version {n, live}` and per-key `data.changed {key, op, by: {kind, name}}`; a lagging consumer gets `pf:resync`.
- [ ] The v0 "being made…" placeholder subscribes to `/_rt/events` and cross-fades to REV 1 with no reload.
- [ ] Data snapshots of shared docs: no policy row = `daily` keep 7 from the first shared write, `hourly` keep 48, `off`; unchanged days skipped; on-demand snapshots (`contribute`, `before_restore`, `before_reset`) outside `keep`; after 90 days unopened keep the last one until the part leaves the bin; roll back and reset atomic, snapshot first, one `data.changed` per affected key; `take_snapshot(part, reason)` for the contribute switch; JSON download.
- [ ] `part_data` op: `get/list/set/delete/snapshot_list/snapshot_restore/reset` with the contract's fields, outputs and errors; `if_rev` CAS (`0` = must not exist); `provenance` + `contains_untrusted`; `request_id` idempotency; snapshot actions need `parts:write` + `edit` and act on shared data only.

## Plan refs
§2 Runtime calls `/_rt`, the prelude; §3a role × runtime matrix, who writes shared data, limits, Can contribute; §3c Persistent state; §4 Events, Slice 1 op fields; §4a.6 "Being made…"; §5c Data snapshots; §5e `data_docs`, `events`, `data_snapshot_policies`, `data_snapshots`; §5h; decisions 26, 31, 43; docs/agent-contract.md "Shared data from inside a part", `part_data`, Rule 6.

## Considerations
- Claude's exact signatures are what let copied artifacts run unchanged; a missing key resolves `null`.
- Track shared bytes with a per-part counter in the writer, never `SUM()` per write.
- Per-key `data.changed` on roll back means pages repaint with no special path; events carry keys, never values.
- Snapshots undo bad writes, they are not DR; never personal docs, never backend volumes. Their blobs are part blobs, so GC and export keep them.
- Under `storage_full`, roll back and reset are refused too (they snapshot first); say so in the hint.
- Can-view link, guest and render principals in tests use test-minted caps; the real link and guest flows are the public-links bead.

## Tests and logging
