title: Workspace, config and CI: the Cargo workspace, the config and secrets loader, CI and Renovate
description:
## Goal
Create the repository skeleton every other bead builds in: one Cargo workspace producing one static binary (`partifactory`, with `part` as a CLI alias, every asset embedded, the build worker the same binary re-exec'd), a crate layout that keeps the core free of vendor adapters, the typed config and secrets loader (the env contract), and a CI pipeline that enforces formatting, lints, tests, licences, advisories and secret scanning from the first commit. A household server is set up once and left alone, so dependency hygiene and safe config have to be automatic from day one.

## Scope
- [ ] Workspace at the root: `resolver = "2"`, pinned `rust-toolchain.toml` (stable + rustfmt + clippy), release profile with `panic = "abort"`, LTO and strip for a ~20 MB `FROM scratch` musl image.
- [ ] Crates (`crates/pf-<name>`, each with a responsibility doc comment): config, db, blobs, model, build, caps, serve, prelude, ops, api, mcp, cli, auth, policy, oauth, ui, obs, janitor, backup, provision, render, runner, adapter-cloudflare, adapter-authentik, and the `partifactory` binary. Directory placeholders `tests/e2e/`, `tests/agent_surfaces/`, `tests/golden/`, `tests/device/`, `docs/spikes/`, `deploy/proxy/`, `examples/ci/`.
- [ ] The binary with `clap` subcommand stubs (`serve`, `build-worker`, `runner`, `export`, `import`, `migrate`, `healthcheck`, `provision`, `doctor`, `deploy`, `config check`, `admin bootstrap`, `admin break-glass`, `bench`, `logs`) and `argv[0] == "part"` dispatching to the CLI.
- [ ] Adapter-boundary check: CI fails if any core crate depends on a `pf-adapter-*` crate.
- [ ] CI as plain scripts (`ci/fmt.sh`, `ci/clippy.sh`, `ci/test.sh`, `ci/deny.sh`, `ci/audit.sh`, `ci/gitleaks.sh`, `ci/check-boundaries.sh`, `ci/env-docs.sh`) plus one thin workflow for the forge in use; nextest profiles `default` and `ci` (JUnit kept as an artifact).
- [ ] Secret scanning (AGENTS.md "Secrets and site config"): gitleaks in CI on every PR and as a pre-push hook installed by `scripts/install-hooks.sh`, with a `.gitleaks.toml` that knows the `pf_at_`, `pf_rt_` and `pf_pat_` token shapes and allowlists the documented fixture values; a planted-secret fixture test proves both the CI job and the hook fail.
- [ ] Section 3h layer 1 from the start: Renovate (Cargo, Dockerfile base images pinned by digest, workflow pins; oxc/rolldown exact-pin only, never automerged), `cargo deny` + `cargo audit` on every PR, and a nightly advisory run on `main`.
- [ ] The config crate: `site.toml` (path `PF_SITE_TOML`, default `/data/site.toml`) as typed `deny_unknown_fields` structs for every section in §5c; every key settable as `PF_<SECTION>_<KEY>` (env wins); secrets env or `PF_*_FILE` only, never in the file; a `Secret<T>` newtype that prints `[redacted]`, has no `Serialize` and zeroizes on drop.
- [ ] `partifactory config check`: loads exactly as `serve` would; missing required secret exits 2 naming the variable; cross-field rules; the `[unsafe]` mechanism (a protection switched off without its `[unsafe]` key fails). Its diagnostics are JSON log lines on stdout (`event="config.check"`), the same shape every later bead's gate asserts on.
- [ ] `docs/env.md` generated from the config structs; CI regenerates it and fails on diff.

## Plan refs
§5 Stack (one static binary, why Rust), §5b Builds and deploys (env contract, CI is an example), §5c site.toml sections, Secrets, Rotation, §5d Maintenance (Dependencies), §3h layer 1, §5f Portability, §5h Safe defaults, decisions 2, 9, 22; AGENTS.md (secrets, gitleaks before every push).

## Considerations
- Required secrets: `PF_SESSION_KEY`, `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY`, `PF_DOMAIN_APEX`, `PF_METRICS_TOKEN`, the OIDC client secret if `[idp]` is set, `PF_RUNNER_KEY` if the runner is on; adapter tokens are optional (§5b).
- `_FILE` contents: trim one trailing newline; an empty file is missing; both `PF_X` and `PF_X_FILE` set is an error, never a silent pick.
- CI is an example, not a dependency: nothing reads a CI vendor's API, and the public mirror runs no Actions and holds no secrets, so the scripts are what matter and run identically on a laptop.
- oxc and rolldown are 0.x Rust APIs: Renovate must never bump them on its own (the compiler spike and the tsx epic pin and vendor them).
- The export age recipient is a public key, not a secret. The offline copy of `site.toml`, the admin pin and the age identity is documented in the `docs/env.md` header.
- gitleaks is the last line, not the first: the `Secret<T>` type and the log redaction (observability bead) keep secrets out of output; gitleaks keeps them out of git. Fixture tokens used in tests are documented in `.gitleaks.toml` so the hook never trains people to bypass it.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/partifactory/tests/cli_smoke.rs::help_lists_subcommands`, `argv0_part_dispatches_to_cli`.
- `ci/check-boundaries.sh` self-test with a fixture adding an adapter dep to `pf-model`; `ci/gitleaks.sh` self-test with a planted `pf_pat_` fixture in a scratch commit (expects a non-zero exit), and the same through the pre-push hook.
- `pf_config::tests::missing_required_secret_exit_2`, `file_secret_equals_env_secret`, `both_env_and_file_is_error`, `file_trailing_newline_trimmed`, `env_overrides_toml` (proptest), `unknown_key_suggests`, `canary_never_in_debug_display_logs_panics` (formats, logs and panics with a `CANARY-` secret and asserts it never appears).
- `ci/env-docs.sh`: regenerate and `git diff --exit-code docs/env.md`.
- Log events from config load: `event="config.loaded" outcome="ok"` and `event="config.check" outcome="missing_secret" var="PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY"` (the variable name, never the value).

## Verification gate
- Observed on the release binary built from `main`: `partifactory --help` lists the stubs; `part` (a symlink) reaches the CLI; `partifactory config check` with a scrubbed env exits 2 naming `PF_SESSION_KEY`; with `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY_FILE` it loads the same value as the env var.
- CI green on `main` with every job visible (fmt, clippy, nextest, deny, audit, gitleaks, boundaries, env-docs); a deliberate fmt break, a clippy warning and a planted secret each failed CI once, then reverted; the nightly advisory job has run on `main`; Renovate has opened a PR against a deliberately outdated pin.
- Logs checked: the release binary's `config check` run with the scrubbed env prints a JSON line `event="config.check" outcome="missing_secret" var="PF_SESSION_KEY"` on stdout; the canary test's captured output contains `event="config.check"` lines and no canary value.
- No regressions: `ci/*.sh` run locally give the same results as CI.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run ids (PR run and nightly run), the Renovate PR link, and the `config check` transcript; `br gate report` for `ci_green` and `verified` before `br close`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CI green on a hello-world binary; `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` run in CI; Renovate opens a PR on a pinned dep
- [ ] Missing required secret -> exit 2 with the env var name; a `_FILE` secret loads identically to the env var; a canary secret never appears in Debug, logs or panics; `docs/env.md` regenerates with no diff in CI
- [ ] Every crate in the layout exists with a responsibility doc comment, and the adapter-boundary check fails when a core crate adds a dependency on `pf-adapter-cloudflare` (verified once).
- [ ] A nightly advisory run (`cargo audit` + `cargo deny check advisories`) runs on `main`, and Renovate pins Dockerfile base images by digest and never automerges oxc or rolldown.
- [ ] Env overrides `site.toml` for every key (`PF_<SECTION>_<KEY>`), and unknown keys in `site.toml` are rejected with a suggestion.
- [ ] A protection switched off without its `[unsafe]` key fails `config check`.
- [ ] gitleaks runs in CI on every PR and as a pre-push hook installed by `scripts/install-hooks.sh`; a planted `pf_pat_` fixture fails both (verified once), and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists only the documented test fixtures.
- [ ] GATE: On the release binary built from `main`, `partifactory --help` lists every stub, `part` reaches the CLI, and `partifactory config check` with a scrubbed env exits 2 naming `PF_SESSION_KEY` (transcript recorded).
- [ ] GATE: CI is green on `main` with fmt, clippy, nextest, deny, audit, gitleaks, boundaries and env-docs as separate jobs; a deliberate fmt break, a clippy warning and a planted secret each failed CI once; the nightly advisory job has run.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the release binary's `config check` run prints the JSON line `event="config.check" outcome="missing_secret" var="PF_SESSION_KEY"` on stdout, and the canary test's captured output has `event="config.check"` lines and no canary value.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: `ci/*.sh` run locally match CI.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run ids, the Renovate PR link, the `config check` transcript) and `ci_green` + `verified` gate reports.

title: Spikes: oxc and rolldown as libraries, rmcp stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos vs askama
description:
## Goal
Three one-day maturity spikes, run in week one beside the sandbox spike, each ending in a go/no-go note with a runnable example. They de-risk the three young dependencies the plan bets on: the TSX compiler (oxc + rolldown as Rust libraries in a child process), the MCP server SDK (rmcp 3.x, stateless Streamable HTTP), and the workspace UI framework (Leptos 0.8 SSR + hydration vs `askama`/`maud` + vanilla-JS islands). The `tsx` kind moved to right after Slice 1, but the compiler spike stays here so an oxc or rolldown problem still shows up first.

## Scope
- [ ] Compiler (`spike-compiler`, note `docs/spikes/compiler.md`): re-exec itself as a child, length-prefixed CBOR over stdin/stdout (the build-child protocol shape); in the child, oxc transforms `App.tsx` (automatic JSX runtime, TS stripping) and rolldown bundles against an in-memory module set (`react`, `react-dom` 18.3, no network, no `node_modules` walk); emit ESM + an import map, minified. Enforce the 10 s deadline, `RLIMIT_AS` 1 GiB and `SIGKILL`; show a hang and a panic reported as failed builds. Measure spawn cost, cold/warm time for three inputs (a 50-line component, a recharts-sized import, five files) and memory peak against the TSX targets (p50 < 150 ms, p99 < 1 s). Try esbuild-as-subprocess through the same protocol. Recommend a vendoring approach.
- [ ] MCP (`spike-mcp`, note `docs/spikes/mcp.md`): axum on `:8080` mounting rmcp's Streamable HTTP service at `/mcp`, stateless, with two toy tools from `deny_unknown_fields` + `JsonSchema` structs. The eight checks: stateless (no session id; `server/discover`, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` of the 2026-07-28 revision); `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` from schemars with non-object outputs wrapped; tool annotations; errors as `isError: true` + `structuredContent` + one text line; auth failure as HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` raised by middleware before rmcp; image content blocks (PNG ≤ 1 MB); long markdown `instructions`; `part://` resources as projections. Connect with `claude mcp add --transport http spike http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer test"` and with rmcp's own client.
- [ ] UI (`spike-ui`, note `docs/spikes/ui.md`): build the share sheet (five-rung ladder, live sentence, Can view / Can contribute switch, Copy, a fake in-sheet step-up) in Leptos and in templates + an island; build the 44 px part-view bar as a hydrated Leptos page and measure its bundle with `brotli -q 11`; a 30-minute CodeMirror 6 interop probe; apply the decision rule.
- [ ] Each note: question, exact crate versions/commits, what was built, measurements, findings, risks, a decision line (go / no-go / go-with-fallback), and what the dependent beads must do differently.

## Plan refs
§5 Stack (TSX/JSX, MCP and Workspace UI rows; "Why Leptos, and when it loses"; "Maturity check before P0 freezes"), §3d The build worker, §4b One operation registry and Adapters, §5a targets, §6 "Why the sandbox and TSX in P0", §6a Spikes, decision 39.

## Considerations
- The decision rule (§5): if the share sheet costs more than a day of framework friction, or the hydrated part-view bundle exceeds 300 KB brotli, use `askama`/`maud` + small vanilla-JS islands. Record friction hours honestly, overruns included. The wrapper stays a tiny standalone bundle with no framework hydration under either option; say how it's built.
- Pin Leptos 0.8.x (0.9 is in release candidates). oxc is 0.x with breaking releases and rolldown's semver promise covers its JS API, not the Rust crate, so pin exactly and vendor.
- Named fallbacks: esbuild-as-subprocess behind the same child protocol (compiler; don't invent a bundler); templates + islands (UI). rmcp has none: a no-go means hand-writing the stateless JSON-RPC endpoint over axum with rmcp's types, and the note says so.
- rmcp's OAuth support is client-side only; the spike only needs bearer extraction. No op may depend on an MCP-only feature (sampling, elicitation, notifications).
- A no-go is a valid outcome. Spike code is throwaway, outside the shipped crates or behind a `spike` feature, never in the release binary; delete it once the dependent beads land.

## Tests and logging
- `spike-compiler/tests/child.rs::{panic_in_child_is_builder_crashed, hang_is_killed_after_deadline, bundle_resolves_virtual_react_once}`.
- `spike-mcp/tests/mcp.rs::{tools_list_schemas_match_schemars, missing_token_is_http_401_not_tool_result, stateless_request_without_session_id_succeeds}`.
- `spike-ui/measure.sh` prints the brotli size; output pasted in the note.
- Logs: `event="build.child" outcome="timeout|builder_crashed|ok"`; `event="http.request" route_class="mcp" status=401` for the token-less call.

## Verification gate
- Three notes merged, each with a decision line, a runnable example and the exact command; a second person (or agent) ran each example and recorded tool and crate versions.
- Observed runs: `cargo run -p spike-compiler -- examples/app.tsx` prints a bundle and an import map; Claude Code lists and calls both `spike-mcp` tools, and a token-less curl gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`; `spike-ui` serves `/leptos` and `/templates` with the measured bundle size.
- CI green on `main` with a job building `-p spike-compiler -p spike-mcp -p spike-ui` and running their tests.
- Logs checked: the child-process test asserts the `event="build.child"` outcomes.
- No regressions: every CI job that exists still passes with the spike job added.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, the transcripts from the notes; `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.

title: Human checks on real devices (non-blocking)
description:
**Human-only, non-blocking. Nothing depends on this bead, and it never blocks a release or another bead. Agents never claim it (`br ready --exclude-label human-only`).**

## Goal
Everything the swarm cannot see from CI, the emulators or the iOS Simulator: the real iPhone, Android and Telegram in-app-browser checks, the by-hand `communal_pixel_editor` run on the example deployment, and the Telegram passkey test with its two decided fixes. The person-bound-link fallback stays rejected.

Every item here has an emulated or simulated stand-in in the bead that ships the feature: Playwright Chromium with mobile emulation and the virtual authenticator, Playwright WebKit with a mobile profile, Playwright Firefox, and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`). title: The trusted wrapper, its chrome API, the content-free card and the Stockroom workspace shell
description:
## Goal
The link to post is the part's own host, `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`. This bead builds what lives there: a trusted, unsandboxed wrapper that frames the sandboxed content at `/c/<cap>/…` with no cap in the address bar, the workspace chrome API it talks to (CORS for exactly the sandboxed part-host origins), the content-free preview card, the Stockroom foundation with the Slice 1 workspace pages, and the wrapper's chrome bar. The share sheet and public links, Connected agents, and the Health page live in their own beads.

## Scope
- [ ] Wrapper at `/` and every path outside `/c/`, `/l/`, `/_pf/`: cap from `#pf=` then `sessionStorage`, else `location.replace` to `/grant?…&mode=wrap`; `share=…` fragments kept across the hop; `history.replaceState` before any other script; sandboxed frame; messages matched by `event.source`; `pf:regrant` answered through the chrome API with no navigation; `<noscript>`; `/_pf/manifest.webmanifest` and icons. Strict wrapper CSP, `no-referrer`, `noindex`, never `Set-Cookie`, identical for every User-Agent.
- [ ] Chrome API `/api/chrome/v1/<part>/…`: `grant`, `summary` (incl. `features`, which drives which controls render), `stepup`. CORS echoes only an active, sandboxed part's own origin on its own routes (credentials, `Vary: Origin`, never `*` or `null`); writes need `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site|same-origin` and JSON. Nothing an agent may do exists only here.
- [ ] Content-free card: two static 1200×630 PNGs (private; "Anyone with the link"), golden files with SVG source, at `/og/<sha256>.png` on the workspace, `public, immutable`; og helper whose text matches the card; card input with no part-derived field.
- [ ] Stockroom foundation: `tokens.css` (light + dark, §4a.3 verbatim), spacing/motion tokens, self-hosted IBM Plex, icon sprite, mark and wordmark, 48 px top bar (theme toggle, avatar menu), CI contrast test.
- [ ] Workspace pages: sign-in (og = private card), gallery (drawer-front cards straight to part hosts, filters, grid/list, day sections, being-made and scratch badges, empty state, skeletons), error pages (404, 403, 410, 429, 500 with request id), 360×740 mobile.
- [ ] Chrome bar: 44 px / 40 px (hides on scroll), back, tag chip, title, name, `REV n`, audience chip, Share, ⋯ (Copy link, Open standalone), corner ticks, cross-fade, the being-made drafting sheet; unsandboxed parts open Share on the workspace.

## Plan refs
§2 The link to post, §2 Serving (framed expiry), §4c Tier (a), §4a.2–4a.7, §4a.9, §5 Leptos decision rule, §7 The wrapper, Chrome-API CORS, Links and cards. Decisions 19, 25, 40.

## Considerations
- UI framework per the Leptos spike; the wrapper bundle is standalone with no hydration either way.
- First open costs one client-side hop (the server never sees the fragment); reloads none.
- CORS never admits an unsandboxed part (same-origin with its wrapper), `blobs`, or a redirecting old name; use the names cache.
- The audience decides the card, never the UA. Static PNGs can't carry the host name, so the card and og text omit it; note it on close.
- Amber only for "Public link"; agents blueprint blue; colour never the only signal; no font CDN, ever (Plex Mono + system sans is the fallback).
- Wrapper and chrome are shared blobs served at serve time, so a platform fix reaches every part on deploy (§3h layer 1).
- Lines needing the share sheet, public links or live `pf:version` are verified in the public links bead.
- This bead needs `/grant`, step-up and the content listener, not the op registry, so it runs in parallel with the registry bead (§6a "/grant → the part-host wrapper and its chrome API"). The chrome API's `summary` is a projection of the same part-service read `part_get` wraps; whichever of the two beads lands second routes it through the registry, so nothing an agent may do exists only here.
- The wrapper first-open and regrant specs also run in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`); real phones never block anything.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/{wrapper_headers,root_ua_independence,chrome_cors_fuzz,chrome_csrf,og_route}.rs`, `pf_serve::og::tests::*`, `crates/pf-ui/tests/contrast.rs`.
- E2E (chromium-desktop + webkit-mobile): `tests/e2e/wrapper_{first_open,fragment,isolation,regrant,chrome}.spec.ts`, `stepup_from_wrapper.spec.ts`, `gallery_open.spec.ts` (HAR: no third-party requests), `tests/e2e/visual/*`.
- Logs: `event="wrapper.serve" audience=…`, `event="chrome.cors" decision="deny"`, `event="chrome.grant"`, `event="og.serve"`, `event="stepup.verify" origin=…`, `event="ui.render" page="gallery"`.

## Verification gate
- Running build in the harness: open `https://pixel-part.pf.test/` from the gallery in one click, one `/grant` hop, clean address bar, no hop on reload; signed-out `curl -si` of the root shows the private card, no cap, no part bytes, no `Set-Cookie`, same bytes for a bot UA; the CORS fuzz against the live server; a workspace passkey asserts from the wrapper; screenshots light, dark, 360 px.
- CI green on `main`: nextest and harness e2e jobs include the tests above.
- Logs: the e2e run asserts `wrapper.serve`, `chrome.grant` and `stepup.verify`.
- No regressions in the full e2e suite.
- Evidence on close plus the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] After first open the address bar shows `https://<name>-part.<domain>/<path>` with no fragment. A reload makes no `/grant` request.
- [ ] A test script inside the part tries `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage` and fails.
- [ ] The wrapper response has the strict wrapper CSP and no `Set-Cookie`. The root contains no cap and no part bytes when signed out.
- [ ] `/_pf/manifest.webmanifest` has `scope: "/"` and `id: "/"`.
- [ ] Root responses are byte-identical for bot and browser User-Agents, and a signed-out root carries the private card og tags.
- [ ] CORS headers are present only for the active, sandboxed part's own origin on its own routes.
- [ ] `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, an old redirecting name, `https://evil.example`, and `http://` variants all get no CORS headers.
- [ ] A write without `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site|same-origin`, or without a JSON body, is refused.
- [ ] `POST …/grant` returns a fresh cap for an allowed viewer and the standard 403/401 shape otherwise.
- [ ] When the cap window passes, the prelude's `pf:regrant` gets a new frame src through the chrome API with no top-level navigation.
- [ ] Both PNGs are golden files with fixed text only; the og:title/og:description on the root and sign-in pages match the card text exactly; the private and public-link variants differ only in the audience line
- [ ] Two PNGs at 1200x630, each <= 150 KB, embedded in the binary, `GET /og/<sha256>.png` serves each with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `image/png` and no `Set-Cookie`, and any other hash returns 404; the card input type has no part-derived field.
- [ ] The contrast test is green, light and dark.
- [ ] Fonts are served from the binary only. No request leaves the workspace origin for fonts (asserted in e2e).
- [ ] The gallery card opens the part host in 1 click.
- [ ] The sign-in page og tags equal the private card text.
- [ ] Visual snapshots at 360 px, light and dark.
- [ ] Copy link copies exactly `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`.
- [ ] The 40 px phone bar hides on scroll. Targets are >= 44x44.
- [ ] The wrapper renders only the controls listed in `summary.features` (Slice 1: Share, Copy link, Open standalone).
- [ ] The wrapper's script and styles are shared blobs referenced at serve time, so a wrapper fix ships with a deploy and needs no part rebuild.
- [ ] Expired cap in a framed part triggers exactly one `pf:regrant` and the page continues without navigation.
- [ ] IdP-admin user gets 403; an admin action without a fresh assertion returns `step_up_required`; a passkey registered on the workspace asserts from a part-host wrapper (virtual authenticator); household sharing never asks; `admin bootstrap` registers a local admin passkey once; break-glass works once within 5 min and is audited
- [ ] A passkey registered on the workspace asserts successfully from a part-host wrapper origin (virtual authenticator in Chromium).
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` in the e2e harness, a signed-in person opens `https://pixel-part.pf.test/` from the gallery in one click with one silent `/grant` hop and a clean address bar, a reload makes no hop, a signed-out `curl -si` of the root returns the private card, no cap, no part bytes and no `Set-Cookie` (identical for a bot UA), and a workspace passkey asserts from the wrapper.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `crates/pf-serve/tests/{wrapper_headers,root_ua_independence,chrome_cors_fuzz,chrome_csrf,og_route}.rs` and `crates/pf-ui/tests/contrast.rs` in the nextest job, and `tests/e2e/wrapper_*.spec.ts`, `gallery_open.spec.ts`, `stepup_from_wrapper.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/visual/*` in the harness e2e job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="wrapper.serve"`, `event="chrome.grant" outcome="ok"` and `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"`.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, curl excerpts, gallery and part-view screenshot paths in light, dark and 360 px) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports recorded.
- [ ] GATE: Simulator lane: `wrapper_first_open` and `wrapper_regrant` pass in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`), with posts, screenshots and the runtime version attached to the `verified` report.

title: P4 Family, Nest and phone: onboarding, embedding, service identities, slides and Mermaid, screenshots, phone editing, OTLP
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Bring the whole family in and meet them where they are: onboarding into the family space, family parts embedded in the Nest (with its own service identity), a family-only Hermes profile, slides and diagrams, screenshot thumbnails, and editing or commenting straight from a phone. Optional OTLP export lands here too.

## Scope
- [ ] Family onboarding: invite into the `family` space (admin, step-up, only for new people), a first-run tour, the personal space created on first sign-in.
- [ ] Embedding: `[embed] frame_ancestors` feeds the part CSP and the wrapper CSP; the embedder frames the part host root or `/c/` with a server-minted `src`; `pf-embed.js` handles `pf:regrant` with no navigation.
- [ ] Service identities: `principal_kind = service`, spaces fixed to `family`, created only by the admin with step-up; writes labelled as the service; `requested_by` recorded and shown as unverified. The Nest's connection first.
- [ ] The Hermes `nest-family` profile: a family-space-only agent profile for the household chat.
- [ ] The `slides` kind (block = slide) plus Mermaid and KaTeX for markdown and slides, client-side from the shared blob host.
- [ ] Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery (600x375 WebP part blobs from the render sidecar) and opt-in screenshot og:images for public links.
- [ ] Phone editing: "Edit text" tap-to-edit as an anchor edit (`old_str` = the original text), falling back to "Ask the agent"; long-press point-and-comment with an anchor `{version, block_id | selector, text_quote, rect}`, over the wrapper <-> part postMessage channel.
- [ ] Optional OTLP export adapter (traces, logs, metrics), off by default, never required.

## Plan refs
§2 Embedding, Framed expiry; §3b Service identities, "Agent consent is limited to spaces"; §3c Phone editing; §4 Example consumers (the Nest); §4a.6 Thumbnails; §4c Tier (b) outputs; §5f Embedding and Telemetry export rows; §5g; §6 P4; §6a P4.

## Considerations
- Live space inheritance is why onboarding works: "everything in Family is the family's" stays true when someone joins later. Granting an existing account is inward; inviting a new person is the admin's.
- Embedding default is empty: only the part's own host and the workspace may frame it. A framed part never navigates itself to `/grant` (a subframe navigation from an opaque origin is cross-site for `SameSite=Lax`, so a sign-in page would render in the frame). Same-site embedders like the Nest get the Lax cookie on the regrant call; cross-site embedders can only use the server-minted `src` path. Document it.
- `versions.author_user` is `NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)`, and a service has no person: recommended is a reserved `local` user row per service (`in_audience = 0`, no passkey, can't sign in). Decide and record it.
- Enforcement for the nest-family profile is the connection's consented spaces, so even a prompt-injected profile can't leave `family`. Hermes is an example consumer; nothing in core depends on it.
- Mermaid and KaTeX run client-side so the build child stays within 10 s with no network, and the CSP doesn't change. The slide shell uses Jig styles.
- Private thumbnails are part blobs, never in a shared cache. The audience decides the card, never the User-Agent; a screenshot card needs that link's opt-in, because unfurlers store images.
- Phone edits are anchor edits, not DOM serialisation: the source stays the diffable truth. The prelude only answers "what is at this point"; the server verifies the proposed `old_str`.
- OTLP exports only already-redacted data; add OTLP payloads to the no-content fuzz test's sinks when enabled.

## Order inside the phase
Family onboarding after native invites (P2b); Nest embedding and service identities; slides and Mermaid after block ids; screenshot thumbnails after the render sidecar and the titled card; phone editing; OTLP (§6a).

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build: a family member opens a Nest-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it on the phone, long-presses to ask Hermes for a change, and Hermes, watching the event log, tells them in its own chat when the fix lands, on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`); the real-phone pass is the non-blocking human-checks bead's.
- CI green on `main` with the embedding, service-identity, slides and phone-editing e2e specs in the harness job.
- Logs checked: the e2e run asserts the service-labelled write (`principal="conn:..."` with the service actor) and the refused non-family write (`outcome="forbidden"`).
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate output, engine and simulator runtime versions, screenshot paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

- [ ] A new family member invited to the space sees all family parts and none of the admin's private parts
- [ ] Allowed origin frames root and `/c/`; disallowed origin is blocked by `frame-ancestors`.
- [ ] Expiring cap in an embedded frame recovers via `pf-embed.js` without a navigation.
- [ ] Default config (empty list) yields exactly `frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace>`.
- [ ] Service connection creatable only by the admin with step-up; spaces fixed to `family`.
- [ ] Service write to a non-family space → `forbidden {space}`.
- [ ] Writes labelled as the service; `requested_by` shown as unverified.
- [ ] The profile can create parts in `family` only; a write elsewhere is refused with `forbidden {space}`
- [ ] Golden slide deck renders; block ops address slides
- [ ] Gallery tiles show screenshots when the sidecar is on and SVG thumbs when it's off; a public link without the opt-in never gets a screenshot card
- [ ] On a phone, a typo fixed by tapping it becomes one `part_edit`; a long-press comment carries `{version, selector|block, quote}`

The real-phone embed check is the human-checks bead's.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build: a family member opens a Nest-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it, long-presses to ask Hermes for a change, and Hermes tells them in its own chat when the fix lands, on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (evidence attached to `verified`); the real-phone pass is the human-checks bead's and never blocks.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the embedding, service-identity, slides and phone-editing e2e specs in the harness job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts the service-labelled write and the refused non-family write (`outcome="forbidden"`).

title: Shipping: the OCI image and compose deliverable, the security suite, the drill and the real-device pass
description:
## Goal
Ship partifactory as three vendor-free things (an amd64 OCI image deployed by digest, `deploy/compose.yaml`, the env contract) with a health-gated `partifactory deploy` that rolls itself back. Then prove it from outside: every section-7 line for what exists runs as a test against the compose deployment through its proxy, a drill restores the newest export on a second OCI host in under 15 minutes, and the device pass runs on emulated and simulated devices (Playwright mobile projects and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator). Real phones never block: the real iPhone, Android and Telegram checks live in the non-blocking human-checks bead.

## Scope
- [ ] Image: `cargo-chef` cached deps, static musl binary with every asset embedded, `FROM scratch` + CA certs, non-root `65532`, builder images pinned by digest, `partifactory healthcheck` (no shell in the image).
- [ ] Release on tag (`scripts/release.sh`, CI-agnostic): pushed image, `release/digest.txt`, `part` CLI binaries, `SHA256SUMS`, forge release assets, `cargo binstall` metadata.
- [ ] `deploy/compose.yaml`: image by digest, `/data` volume, `8080`/`8081` to the proxy only, `9090` local only, `_FILE` secrets, the `render` profile (the sidecar service definition from the part_check bead, carried into the published file), `proxy` profile (the one `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` + maintenance page), `json-file` 10m x 3 on every service; `deploy/.env.example`, `scripts/check_env_contract.sh`, `docs/host.md`.
- [ ] `partifactory deploy`: record previous digest, pull, forward-only `migrate`, start beside the old one, wait for `/readyz`, switch, watch 2 minutes, roll back on failure; Docker or Podman, `--host ssh://`.
- [ ] Section-7 suite `tests/security/` + `checklist.yaml` (stable id per line mapped to a test, a `covered_by` test, a manual record, or `pending` with its owning bead; the real-device line maps to the human-checks bead as `manual`); raw-request client, Playwright on three engines plus the mobile projects, a canary sibling service, open-redirect and CORS fuzzers; runs from outside against the compose deployment through Caddy in the e2e harness. The same suite is runnable against any deployment (`--base-url`), which the human-checks bead uses for the example deployment.
- [ ] Drill `scripts/drill.sh`: export + image from the release assets + the offline site config into a throwaway stack on a second OCI host (in CI a second Docker context or daemon; from a laptop for the human-checks run), e2e suite, `backup/drills/<ts>.json`, `pf_last_drill_ok` / `pf_last_drill_age_s`, Health drill row; `docs/ops/moving.md`, `docs/ops/backup.md`.
- [ ] Device-emulation pass `tests/device/`: `device-pass.spec.ts` on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` for standalone open, part-host open (first open and reload), the `/l/` guest open and sign-in with the virtual authenticator; `ios-sim.sh device-pass` runs the same self-reporting pages in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator and records posts and screenshots; `tests/manual/real-device-pass.md` stays as the script the human-checks bead follows, with `scripts/check_manual_records.sh` validating its result files when they exist.

## Plan refs
§5b Builds and deploys, §3 Topology, §5c drills and moving hosts, §5h, §7 (all but Backends and advisories), §2 Telegram decision, §3a UX; Slice 1 "Shipping it" and definition of done items 4 and 5; decisions 22, 36, 42.

## Considerations
- Never `:latest`. Migrations stay forward-compatible with the previous binary (rollback runs the old binary on the migrated DB). `/readyz` ignores the IdP. Each deploy bumps the boot epoch: open tabs re-grant once, silently.
- Deferred (decision 42, rest of P1): arm64, SBOM, `cosign`, nginx/Traefik, example CI workflows. The runner joins compose with P2a.
- From outside because a proxy forwarding `:9090`, trusting a spoofed client-IP header or caching private blobs only shows through the real ingress. Assert the canonical CSP byte for byte; fuzz `/grant` (`//evil`, `\\evil`, `%2f%2f`, `@evil`, CRLF) and chrome-API origins (`null`, `blobs-part`, renamed names, lookalikes).
- Adapter lines and portability-lane runs come after Slice 1; the two old lines that need the portability lane are verified in the rest-of-P1 epic. Backend lines are P2a; advisory lines the advisories epic. The run against the example deployment (its tunnel, its IdP) is the admin's and lives in the human-checks bead; nothing here waits on it.
- The drill is also the migration test. In CI it runs against a second Docker context so "another OCI host" is real at the daemon level; the laptop run against a physically separate host is the human-checks bead's, because the CI system may be on the host that died.
- Telegram (decision 36) stays decided: the fixes on a failure are set Telegram to open links in the normal browser (`docs/ops/telegram.md`) and make Hermes hint "open in browser". The test itself is a real-phone check and belongs to the human-checks bead; this bead approximates the webview with the WebKit lanes and never builds the rejected person-bound-link fallback. No personal data in result files.
